===== M0029 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PureFunctionIdentifier.propagateSideEffects()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PureFunctionIdentifier.java
Original range: 252-302
Documentation:
/**
   * Propagate side effect information by building a graph based on
   * call site information stored in FunctionInformation and the
   * DefinitionProvider and then running GraphReachability to
   * determine the set of functions that have side effects.
   */
Method code:
252 |   private void propagateSideEffects() {
253 |     // Nodes are function declarations; Edges are function call sites.
254 |     DiGraph<FunctionInformation, Node> sideEffectGraph =
255 |         LinkedDirectedGraph.createWithoutAnnotations();
256 | 
257 |     // create graph nodes
258 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
259 |       sideEffectGraph.createNode(functionInfo);
260 |     }
261 | 
262 |     // add connections to called functions and side effect root.
263 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
264 |       if (!functionInfo.mayHaveSideEffects()) {
265 |         continue;
266 |       }
267 | 
268 |       for (Node callSite : functionInfo.getCallsInFunctionBody()) {
269 |         Node callee = callSite.getFirstChild();
270 |         Collection<Definition> defs =
271 |             getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider, callee);
272 |         if (defs == null) {
273 |           // Definition set is not complete or eligible.  Possible
274 |           // causes include:
275 |           //  * "callee" is not of type NAME or GETPROP.
276 |           //  * One or more definitions are not functions.
277 |           //  * One or more definitions are complex.
278 |           //    (e.i. return value of a call that returns a function).
279 |           functionInfo.setTaintsUnknown();
280 |           break;
281 |         }
282 | 
283 |         for (Definition def : defs) {
284 |           Node defValue = def.getRValue();
285 |           FunctionInformation dep = functionSideEffectMap.get(defValue);
286 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(dep);
287 |           sideEffectGraph.connect(dep, callSite, functionInfo);
288 |         }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 | 
292 |     // Propagate side effect information to a fixed point.
293 |     FixedPointGraphTraversal.newTraversal(new SideEffectPropagationCallback())
294 |         .computeFixedPoint(sideEffectGraph);
295 | 
296 |     // Mark remaining functions "pure".
297 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
298 |       if (functionInfo.mayBePure()) {
299 |         functionInfo.setIsPure();
300 |       }
301 |     }
302 |   }

===== M0030 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // Ok, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
101 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.createNameInformation(String,Scope,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1430-1457
Documentation:
/**
   * Creates name information for a particular qualified name that occurs in a
   * particular scope.
   *
   * @param name A qualified name (e.g. "x" or "a.b.c")
   * @param scope The scope in which {@code name} occurs
   * @param rootNameNode The NAME node for the first token of {@code name}
   * @return The name information, or null if the name is irrelevant to this
   *     pass
   */
Method code:
1430 |   private NameInformation createNameInformation(
1431 |       String name, Scope scope, Node rootNameNode) {
1432 |     // Check the scope. Currently we're only looking at globally scoped vars.
1433 |     String rootName = rootNameNode.getString();
1434 |     Var v = scope.getVar(rootName);
1435 |     boolean isExtern = (v == null && externalNames.contains(rootName));
1436 |     boolean isGlobalRef = (v != null && v.isGlobal()) || isExtern ||
1437 |         rootName.equals(WINDOW);
1438 |     if (!isGlobalRef) {
1439 |       return null;
1440 |     }
1441 | 
1442 |     NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1443 | 
1444 |     // If a prototype property or method, fill in prototype information.
1445 |     int idx = name.indexOf(PROTOTYPE_SUBSTRING);
1446 |     if (idx != -1) {
1447 |       nameInfo.isPrototype = true;
1448 |       nameInfo.prototypeClass = name.substring(0, idx);
1449 |       nameInfo.prototypeProperty = name.substring(
1450 |           idx + PROTOTYPE_SUBSTRING_LEN);
1451 |     }
1452 | 
1453 |     nameInfo.name = name;
1454 |     nameInfo.isExternallyReferenceable =
1455 |         isExtern || isExternallyReferenceable(scope, name);
1456 |     return nameInfo;
1457 |   }

/**
   * Computes the list of subtrees whose root nodes have side effects.
   *
   * <p>If the current subtree's root has side effects this method should
   * call accumulator.keepSubTree and return 'false' to add the
   * subtree to the result list and avoid avoid traversing the nodes children.
   *
   * <p>Branching nodes whose then or else branch contain side effects
   * must be simplified by doing a recursive traversal; this method
   * should call the appropriate accumulator 'keepSimplified' method
   * and return 'false' to stop the regular traversal.
   */
Method code:
221 |   @Override
222 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
223 |       NodeTraversal traversal, Node node, Node parent) {
224 |     if (FORBIDDEN_TYPES.contains(node.getType()) ||
225 |         NodeUtil.isControlStructure(node)) {
226 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException(
227 |           Token.name(node.getType()) + " nodes are not supported.");
228 |     }
229 | 
230 |     // Do not recurse into nested functions.
231 |     if (node.isFunction()) {
232 |       return false;
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // simplify and maybe keep hook expression.
236 |     if (node.isHook()) {
237 |       return processHook(node);
238 |     }
239 | 
240 |     // simplify and maybe keep AND/OR expression.
241 |     if ((node.isAnd()) || (node.isOr())) {
242 |       return processShortCircuitExpression(node);
243 |     }
244 | 
245 |     if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(node)) {
246 |       return true;
247 |     } else {
248 | 
249 |       // Node type suggests that the expression has side effects.
250 | 
251 |       if (node.isCall()) {
252 |         return processFunctionCall(node);
253 |       } else if (node.isNew()) {
254 |         return processConstructorCall(node);
255 |       } else {
256 |         accumulator.keepSubTree(node);
257 |         return false;
258 |       }
259 |     }
260 |   }

===== M0041 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.topologicalStableSort(List<T>,Multimap<T, T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java
Original range: 239-288
Documentation:

Method code:
239 |   private static <T> List<T> topologicalStableSort(
240 |       List<T> items, Multimap<T, T> deps) {
241 |     if (items.size() == 0) {
242 |       // Priority queue blows up if we give it a size of 0. Since we need
243 |       // to special case this either way, just bail out.
244 |       return Lists.newArrayList();
245 |     }
246 | 
247 |     final Map<T, Integer> originalIndex = Maps.newHashMap();
248 |     for (int i = 0; i < items.size(); i++) {
249 |       originalIndex.put(items.get(i), i);
250 |     }
251 | 
252 |     PriorityQueue<T> inDegreeZero = new PriorityQueue<T>(items.size(),
253 |         new Comparator<T>() {
254 |       @Override
255 |       public int compare(T a, T b) {
256 |         return originalIndex.get(a).intValue() -
257 |             originalIndex.get(b).intValue();
258 |       }
259 |     });
260 |     List<T> result = Lists.newArrayList();
261 | 
262 |     Multiset<T> inDegree = HashMultiset.create();
263 |     Multimap<T, T> reverseDeps = ArrayListMultimap.create();
264 |     Multimaps.invertFrom(deps, reverseDeps);
265 | 
266 |     // First, add all the inputs with in-degree 0.
267 |     for (T item : items) {
268 |       Collection<T> itemDeps = deps.get(item);
269 |       inDegree.add(item, itemDeps.size());
270 |       if (itemDeps.isEmpty()) {
271 |         inDegreeZero.add(item);
272 |       }
273 |     }
274 | 
275 |     // Then, iterate to a fixed point over the reverse dependency graph.
276 |     while (!inDegreeZero.isEmpty()) {
277 |       T item = inDegreeZero.remove();
278 |       result.add(item);
279 |       for (T inWaiting : reverseDeps.get(item)) {
280 |         inDegree.remove(inWaiting, 1);
281 |         if (inDegree.count(inWaiting) == 0) {
282 |           inDegreeZero.add(inWaiting);
283 |         }
284 |       }
285 |     }
286 | 
287 |     return result;
288 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 683-733
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
683 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
684 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
685 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
686 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
687 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
688 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
689 |         return false;
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
693 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
694 |       // checked.
695 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
696 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
697 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
698 |           return false;
699 |         }
700 | 
701 |         if (refDecl != refInit) {
702 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
703 |           startingReadRef = 2;
704 |         }
705 | 
706 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
707 |           return false;
708 |         }
709 | 
710 |         Node value = refInit.getAssignedValue();
711 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
712 | 
713 |         boolean isImmutableValueWorthInlining =
714 |             NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
715 |             (!value.isString() ||
716 |                 isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references));
717 |         boolean isInlinableThisAlias =
718 |             value.isThis() &&
719 |             !refInfo.isEscaped();
720 |         if (!isImmutableValueWorthInlining && !isInlinableThisAlias) {
721 |           return false;
722 |         }
723 |       }
724 | 
725 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
726 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
727 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
728 |           return false;
729 |         }
730 |       }
731 | 
732 |       return true;
733 |     }

286 |     @Override
287 |     public  void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
288 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
289 |       if (refInfo != null) {
290 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
291 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
292 |         String fullName = name.getFullName();
293 |         switch (ref.type) {
294 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
295 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
296 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
297 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
298 |             if (valParent.isAssign() && name.isSimpleName() &&
299 |                 name.getDeclaration() == ref) {
300 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
301 |               // before it's declared
302 |               compiler.report(
303 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
304 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
305 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
306 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
307 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
308 | 
309 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
310 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
311 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
312 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |           default:
316 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
317 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
318 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
319 |               // or it's an error.
320 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
321 |               if (info != null) {
322 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
323 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
324 |               }
325 |             }
326 |             break;
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 | 
330 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
331 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
332 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
333 |         compiler.report(
334 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
335 |       }
336 | 
337 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
338 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
339 |         if (n.isAssign()) {
340 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
341 |           n.removeChild(last);
342 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
343 |         } else {
344 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.isName());
345 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
346 |         }
347 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
348 |       }
349 | 
350 |       if (n.isCall()) {
351 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
352 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
353 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
354 |           //
355 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
356 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
357 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
358 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
359 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, expecially because
360 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
361 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
362 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
363 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
364 |           }
365 |

367 |         }
368 |       }
369 |

371 |     }

/**
   * Gets all the dependencies of the given roots. The inputs must be returned
   * in a stable order. In other words, if A comes before B, and A does not
   * transitively depend on B, then A must also come before B in the returned
   * list.
   *
   * @param sorted If true, get them in topologically sorted order. If false,
   *     get them in the original order they were passed to the compiler.
   */
Method code:
210 |   public List<INPUT> getDependenciesOf(List<INPUT> roots, boolean sorted) {
211 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(inputs.containsAll(roots));
212 |     Set<INPUT> included = Sets.newHashSet();
213 |     Deque<INPUT> worklist = new ArrayDeque<INPUT>(roots);
214 |     while (!worklist.isEmpty()) {
215 |       INPUT current = worklist.pop();
216 |       if (included.add(current)) {
217 |         for (String req : current.getRequires()) {
218 |           INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
219 |           if (dep != null) {
220 |             worklist.add(dep);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |     }
225 | 
226 |     ImmutableList.Builder<INPUT> builder = ImmutableList.builder();
227 |     for (INPUT current : (sorted ? sortedList : inputs)) {
228 |       if (included.contains(current)) {
229 |         builder.add(current);
230 |       }
231 |     }
232 |     return builder.build();
233 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineSimpleMethods.InlineTrivialAccessors.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineSimpleMethods.java

Method code:
67 |     @Override
68 |     void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node callNode, Node parent, String callName) {
69 |       if (externMethods.contains(callName) ||
70 |           nonMethodProperties.contains(callName)) {
71 |         return;
72 |       }
73 | 
74 |       Collection<Node> definitions = methodDefinitions.get(callName);
75 |       if (definitions == null || definitions.size() == 0) {
76 |         return;
77 |       }
78 | 
79 |       // Do check of arity, complexity, and consistency in what we think is
80 |       // the order from least to most complex
81 |       Node firstDefinition = definitions.iterator().next();
82 | 
83 |       // Check any multiple definitions
84 |       if (definitions.size() == 1 || allDefinitionsEquivalent(definitions)) {
85 |

87 |           // Verify this is a trivial return
88 |           Node returned = returnedExpression(firstDefinition);
89 |           if (returned != null) {
90 |             if (isPropertyTree(returned)) {
91 |               logger.fine("Inlining property accessor: " + callName);
92 |               inlinePropertyReturn(parent, callNode, returned);
93 |             } else if (NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(returned, false) &&
94 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(callNode.getFirstChild())) {
95 |               logger.fine("Inlining constant accessor: " + callName);
96 |               inlineConstReturn(parent, callNode, returned);
97 |             }
98 |           } else if (isEmptyMethod(firstDefinition) &&
99 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(callNode.getFirstChild())) {
100 |             logger.fine("Inlining empty method: " + callName);
101 |             inlineEmptyMethod(t, parent, callNode);
102 |           }
103 |         }
104 |       } else {
105 |         logger.fine("Method '" + callName + "' has conflicting definitions.");
106 |       }
107 |     }

/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
225 |   private void computeMustDef(
226 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
227 |     switch (n.getType()) {
228 | 
229 |       case Token.BLOCK:
230 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
231 |         return;
232 | 
233 |       case Token.WHILE:
234 |       case Token.DO:
235 |       case Token.IF:
236 |         computeMustDef(
237 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
238 |         return;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FOR:
241 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
242 |           computeMustDef(
243 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
244 |         } else {
245 |           // for(x in y) {...}
246 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
247 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
248 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
249 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
250 |           }
251 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
252 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.AND:
258 |       case Token.OR:
259 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
260 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
261 |         return;
262 | 
263 |       case Token.HOOK:
264 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
265 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
266 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
267 |         return;
268 | 
269 |       case Token.VAR:
270 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
271 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
272 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
273 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
274 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
275 |           }
276 |         }
277 |         return;
278 | 
279 |       default:
280 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
281 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
282 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
283 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
284 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
285 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
286 |             return;
287 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
288 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
289 |             // parameters itself.
290 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
291 |             if (obj.isName() && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
292 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
293 |               // ie: We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
294 |               // number.
295 |               escapeParameters(output);
296 |             }
297 |           }
298 |         }
299 | 
300 |         if (n.isName() && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
301 |           escapeParameters(output);
302 |         }
303 | 
304 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
305 |         if (n.isDec() || n.isInc()) {
306 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
307 |           if (target.isName()) {
308 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
309 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
310 |             return;
311 |           }
312 |         }
313 | 
314 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
315 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
316 |         }
317 |     }
318 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)

148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);

120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

207 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
208 |     if (parent != null) {
209 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
210 |         case Token.DO:

Method code:
1730 |   private Node parseBasicTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {

===== M0192 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 704-753
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
704 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
705 |     boolean changes = false;
706 |     do {
707 |       changes = false;
708 | 
709 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
710 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
711 |       // we traverse it.
712 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
713 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
714 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
715 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
716 |           current--;
717 |         } else {
718 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
719 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
720 | 
721 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
722 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
723 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
724 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
725 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
726 |           } else {
727 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
728 |             // or a for...in variable.
729 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
730 |           }
731 | 
732 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
733 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
734 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
735 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
736 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
737 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
738 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
739 |             }
740 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
741 |               maybeEscaped = true;
742 |             }
743 |           }
744 | 
745 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
746 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
747 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
748 |             current--;
749 |           }
750 |         }
751 |       }
752 |     } while (changes);
753 |   }

===== M0205 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 152-237
Documentation:

Method code:
152 |   private void computeMayUse(
153 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
154 |     switch (n.getType()) {
155 | 
156 |       case Token.BLOCK:
157 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
158 |         return;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.NAME:
161 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
162 |         return;
163 | 
164 |       case Token.WHILE:
165 |       case Token.DO:
166 |       case Token.IF:
167 |         computeMayUse(
168 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
169 |         return;
170 | 
171 |       case Token.FOR:
172 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
173 |           computeMayUse(
174 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
175 |         } else {
176 |           // for(x in y) {...}
177 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
178 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
179 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
180 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
181 |           }
182 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
183 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
184 |           }
185 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
186 |         }
187 |         return;
188 | 
189 |       case Token.AND:
190 |       case Token.OR:
191 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
192 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
193 |         return;
194 | 
195 |       case Token.HOOK:
196 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
197 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
198 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
199 |         return;
200 | 
201 |       case Token.VAR:
202 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
203 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
204 | 
205 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
206 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
207 |           if (!conditional) {
208 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
209 |           }
210 |         }
211 |         return;
212 | 
213 |       default:
214 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
215 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
216 |           if (!conditional) {
217 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
221 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
222 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
223 |           }
224 | 
225 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
226 |         } else {
227 |           /*
228 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
229 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
230 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
231 |            */
232 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
233 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
234 |           }
235 |         }
236 |     }
237 |   }

===== M0240 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSModuleGraph.manageDependencies(DependencyOptions,List<CompilerInput>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/JSModuleGraph.java
Original range: 311-390
Documentation:
/**
   * Apply the dependency options to the list of sources, returning a new
   * source list re-ordering and dropping files as necessary.
   * This module graph will be updated to reflect the new list.
   *
   * @param inputs The original list of sources. Used to ensure that the sort
   *     is stable.
   * @throws CircularDependencyException if there is a circular dependency
   *     between the provides and requires.
   * @throws MissingProvideException if an entry point was not provided
   *     by any of the inputs.
   * @see DependencyOptions for more info on how this works.
   */
Method code:
311 |   public List<CompilerInput> manageDependencies(
312 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
313 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs)
314 |       throws CircularDependencyException, MissingProvideException {
315 | 
316 |     SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter =
317 |         new SortedDependencies<CompilerInput>(inputs);
318 |     Set<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
319 |     if (depOptions.shouldPruneDependencies()) {
320 |       if (!depOptions.shouldDropMoochers()) {
321 |         entryPointInputs.addAll(sorter.getInputsWithoutProvides());
322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       for (String entryPoint : depOptions.getEntryPoints()) {
325 |         entryPointInputs.add(sorter.getInputProviding(entryPoint));
326 |       }
327 | 
328 |       CompilerInput baseJs = sorter.maybeGetInputProviding("goog");
329 |       if (baseJs != null) {
330 |         entryPointInputs.add(baseJs);
331 |       }
332 |     } else {
333 |       entryPointInputs.addAll(inputs);
334 |     }
335 | 
336 |     // The order of inputs, sorted independently of modules.
337 |     List<CompilerInput> absoluteOrder =
338 |         sorter.getDependenciesOf(inputs, depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
339 | 
340 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module.
341 |     ListMultimap<JSModule, CompilerInput> entryPointInputsPerModule =
342 |         LinkedListMultimap.create();
343 |     for (CompilerInput input : entryPointInputs) {
344 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
345 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(module);
346 |       entryPointInputsPerModule.put(module, input);
347 |     }
348 | 
349 |     // Clear the modules of their inputs. This also nulls out
350 |     // the input's reference to its module.
351 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
352 |       module.removeAll();
353 |     }
354 | 
355 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module, or in one
356 |     // of that module's dependencies.
357 |     for (JSModule module : entryPointInputsPerModule.keySet()) {
358 |       List<CompilerInput> transitiveClosure =
359 |           sorter.getDependenciesOf(
360 |               entryPointInputsPerModule.get(module),
361 |               depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
362 |       for (CompilerInput input : transitiveClosure) {
363 |         JSModule oldModule = input.getModule();
364 |         if (oldModule == null) {
365 |           input.setModule(module);
366 |         } else {
367 |           input.setModule(null);
368 |           input.setModule(
369 |               getDeepestCommonDependencyInclusive(oldModule, module));
370 |         }
371 |       }
372 |     }
373 | 
374 |     // All the inputs are pointing to the modules that own them. Yeah!
375 |     // Update the modules to reflect this.
376 |     for (CompilerInput input : absoluteOrder) {
377 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
378 |       if (module != null) {
379 |         module.add(input);
380 |       }
381 |     }
382 | 
383 |     // Now, generate the sorted result.
384 |     List<CompilerInput> result = Lists.newArrayList();
385 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
386 |       result.addAll(module.getInputs());
387 |     }
388 | 
389 |     return result;
390 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.inlineNonConstants(Var,ReferenceCollection,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 254-323
Documentation:

Method code:
254 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
255 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo,
256 |         boolean maybeModifiedArguments) {
257 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
258 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
259 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
260 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
261 | 
262 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
263 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
264 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
265 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
266 |         Node value;
267 |         if (init != null) {
268 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
269 |         } else {
270 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
271 |           Node srcLocation = declaration.getNode();
272 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(srcLocation);
273 |         }
274 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
275 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
276 |         staleVars.add(v);
277 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
278 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
279 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
280 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
281 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
282 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
283 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
284 |           staleVars.add(v);
285 |         }
286 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
287 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
288 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
289 |           // the variable declaration.
290 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
291 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
292 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
293 |           staleVars.add(v);
294 |         }
295 |       }
296 | 
297 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
298 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
299 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
300 |       // the next pass.)
301 |       if (!maybeModifiedArguments &&
302 |           !staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
303 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
304 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
305 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
306 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNode();
307 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
308 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
309 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias) &&
310 |                 !isVarInlineForbidden(candidate.alias)) {
311 |               Reference aliasInit;
312 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
313 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
314 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
315 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,
316 |                   value,
317 |                   candidate.refInfo.references);
318 |               staleVars.add(candidate.alias);
319 |             }
320 |           }
321 |         }
322 |       }
323 |     }

227 |   private Node tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(Node n) {

===== M0254 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.check()

===== M0285 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

===== M0314 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 508-539
Documentation:
/**
   * Remove duplicate exits.  If the node following the exit node expression
   * has the same effect as exit node, the node can be removed.
   * For example:
   *   "if (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "if (a) {} return f();"
   *   "if (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "if (a) {} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
508 |   private Node tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node n) {
509 |     Node exitExpr = n.getFirstChild();
510 | 
511 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(n);
512 | 
513 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the fall through and return
514 |     // will also trigger all the finally blocks.
515 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
516 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
517 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
518 |       // There were finally clauses
519 |       if (!isPure(exitExpr)) {
520 |         // Can't replace the return
521 |         return n;
522 |       }
523 |     }
524 | 
525 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || exitExpr != null)) {
526 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
527 |       return n;
528 |     }
529 | 
530 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
531 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
532 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
533 |       n.detachFromParent();
534 |       reportCodeChange();
535 |       return null;
536 |     }
537 | 
538 |     return n;
539 |   }

804 |       throw new Error("Missing BLOCK child.");
805 |     }
806 | 
807 |     // Strip unneeded blocks, that is blocks with <2 children unless
808 |     // the CodePrinter specifically wants to keep them.
809 |     if (n.isBlock()) {
810 |       int count = getNonEmptyChildCount(n, 2);
811 |       if (count == 0) {
812 |         if (cc.shouldPreserveExtraBlocks()) {
813 |           cc.beginBlock();
814 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
815 |         } else {
816 |           cc.endStatement(true);
817 |         }
818 |         return;
819 |       }
820 | 
821 |       if (count == 1) {
822 |         // Hack around a couple of browser bugs:
823 |         //   Safari needs a block around function declarations.
824 |         //   IE6/7 needs a block around DOs.
825 |         Node firstAndOnlyChild = getFirstNonEmptyChild(n);
826 |         boolean alwaysWrapInBlock = cc.shouldPreserveExtraBlocks();
827 |         if (alwaysWrapInBlock || isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(firstAndOnlyChild)) {
828 |           cc.beginBlock();
829 |           add(firstAndOnlyChild, Context.STATEMENT);
830 |           cc.maybeLineBreak();
831 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
832 |           return;
833 |         } else {
834 |           // Continue with the only child.
835 |           nodeToProcess = firstAndOnlyChild;
836 |         }
837 |       }
838 | 
839 |       if (count > 1) {
840 |         context = Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
841 |       }
842 |     }
843 | 
844 |     if (nodeToProcess.isEmpty()) {
845 |       cc.endStatement(true);
846 |     } else {
847 |       add(nodeToProcess, context);
848 | 
849 |       // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions - so any
850 |       // VAR in a statement context needs a call to endStatement() here.
851 |       if (nodeToProcess.isVar()) {
852 |         cc.endStatement();
853 |       }
854 |     }
855 |   }

===== M0379 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureCodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureCodingConvention.java
Original range: 74-129
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>Understands several different inheritance patterns that occur in
   * Google code (various uses of {@code inherits} and {@code mixin}).
   */
Method code:
74 |   @Override
75 |   public SubclassRelationship getClassesDefinedByCall(Node callNode) {
76 |     Node callName = callNode.getFirstChild();
77 |     SubclassType type = typeofClassDefiningName(callName);
78 |     if (type != null) {
79 |       Node subclass = null;
80 |       Node superclass = callNode.getLastChild();
81 | 
82 |       // There are six possible syntaxes for a class-defining method:
83 |       // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
84 |       // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
85 |       // goog$inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
86 |       // SubClass.mixin(SuperClass.prototype)
87 |       // goog.mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
88 |       // goog$mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
89 |       boolean isDeprecatedCall = callNode.getChildCount() == 2 &&
90 |           callName.isGetProp();
91 |       if (isDeprecatedCall) {
92 |         // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
93 |         subclass = callName.getFirstChild();
94 |       } else if (callNode.getChildCount() == 3) {
95 |         // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
96 |         subclass = callName.getNext();
97 |       } else {
98 |         return null;
99 |       }
100 | 
101 |       if (type == SubclassType.MIXIN) {
102 |         // Only consider mixins that mix two prototypes as related to
103 |         // inheritance.
104 |         if (!endsWithPrototype(superclass)) {
105 |           return null;
106 |         }
107 |         if (!isDeprecatedCall) {
108 |           if (!endsWithPrototype(subclass)) {
109 |             return null;
110 |           }
111 |           // Strip off the prototype from the name.
112 |           subclass = subclass.getFirstChild();
113 |         }
114 |         superclass = superclass.getFirstChild();
115 |       }
116 | 
117 |       // bail out if either of the side of the "inherits"
118 |       // isn't a real class name. This prevents us from
119 |       // doing something weird in cases like:
120 |       // goog.inherits(MySubClass, cond ? SuperClass1 : BaseClass2)
121 |       if (subclass != null &&
122 |           subclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
123 |           superclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
124 |         return new SubclassRelationship(type, subclass, superclass);
125 |       }
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     return null;
129 |   }

639 |           return newNode(Token.EXPR_RESULT, Node.newNumber(0));

653 |         // same line as the function keyword.
654 |         int lpColumn = functionNode.getAbsolutePosition() +
655 |             functionNode.getLp();

663 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
664 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
665 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
666 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
667 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
668 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
669 |       if (fnName != null) {
670 |         lp.setLineno(fnName.getLineno());
671 |       } else {

673 |       }
674 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
675 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
676 | 
677 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
678 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
679 |         Node paramNode = transform(param);
680 |         // When in ideMode Rhino can generate a param list with only a single
681 |         // ErrorNode. This is transformed into an EMPTY node. Drop this node in
682 |         // ideMode to keep the AST in a valid state.
683 |         if (paramNode.isName()) {

685 |         } else {

/**
   * Returns true if calls to this function have side effects.
   *
   * @param callNode The call node to inspected.
   * @param compiler A compiler object to provide program state changing
   *     context information. Can be null.
   */
Method code:
989 |   static boolean functionCallHasSideEffects(
990 |       Node callNode, @Nullable AbstractCompiler compiler) {
991 |     if (!callNode.isCall()) {
992 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
993 |           "Expected CALL node, got " + Token.name(callNode.getType()));
994 |     }
995 | 
996 |     if (callNode.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
997 |       return false;
998 |     }
999 | 
1000 |     Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
1001 | 
1002 |     // Built-in functions with no side effects.
1003 |     if (nameNode.isName()) {
1004 |       String name = nameNode.getString();
1005 |       if (BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(name)) {
1006 |         return false;
1007 |       }
1008 |     } else if (nameNode.isGetProp()) {
1009 |       if (callNode.hasOneChild()
1010 |           && OBJECT_METHODS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(
1011 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1012 |         return false;
1013 |       }
1014 | 
1015 |       if (callNode.isOnlyModifiesThisCall()
1016 |           && evaluatesToLocalValue(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
1017 |         return false;
1018 |       }
1019 | 
1020 |       // Math.floor has no sideeffects.
1021 |       // TODO(nicksantos): This is a terrible terrible hack, until
1022 |       // I create a definitionprovider that understands namespacing.
1023 |       if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isName()) {
1024 |         if ("Math.floor".equals(nameNode.getQualifiedName())) {
1025 |           return false;
1026 |         }
1027 |       }
1028 | 
1029 |       if (compiler != null && !compiler.hasRegExpGlobalReferences()) {
1030 |         if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isRegExp()
1031 |             && REGEXP_METHODS.contains(nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1032 |           return false;
1033 |         } else if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isString()
1034 |             && STRING_REGEXP_METHODS.contains(
1035 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1036 |           Node param = nameNode.getNext();
1037 |           if (param != null &&
1038 |               (param.isString() || param.isRegExp()))
1039 |           return false;
1040 |         }
1041 |       }
1042 |     }
1043 | 
1044 |     return true;
1045 |   }

249 |     @Override
250 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
251 |       if (n.isGetProp()) {
252 |         String propName = n.getFirstChild().getNext().getString();
253 | 
254 |         if (n.isQualifiedName()) {
255 |           if (propName.equals("prototype")) {
256 |             if (processPrototypeRef(t, n)) {
257 |               return;
258 |             }
259 |           } else if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(propName)) {
260 |             addGlobalUseOfSymbol(propName, t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
261 |             return;
262 |           } else {
263 |             // Do not mark prototype prop assigns as a 'use' in the global scope.
264 |             if (n.getParent().isAssign() && n.getNext() != null) {
265 |               String rValueName = getPrototypePropertyNameFromRValue(n);
266 |               if (rValueName != null) {
267 |                 return;
268 |               }
269 |             }
270 |           }
271 |         }
272 | 
273 |         addSymbolUse(propName, t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
274 |       } else if (n.isObjectLit()) {
275 |         // Make sure that we're not handling object literals being
276 |         // assigned to a prototype, as in:
277 |         // Foo.prototype = {bar: 3, baz: 5};
278 |         String lValueName = NodeUtil.getBestLValueName(
279 |             NodeUtil.getBestLValue(n));
280 |         if (lValueName != null && lValueName.endsWith(".prototype")) {
281 |           return;
282 |         }
283 | 
284 |         // var x = {a: 1, b: 2}
285 |         // should count as a use of property a and b.
286 |         for (Node propNameNode = n.getFirstChild(); propNameNode != null;
287 |              propNameNode = propNameNode.getNext()) {
288 |           // May be STRING, GET, or SET, but NUMBER isn't interesting.
289 |           if (!propNameNode.isQuotedString()) {
290 |             addSymbolUse(propNameNode.getString(), t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
291 |           }
292 |         }
293 |       } else if (n.isName()) {
294 |         String name = n.getString();
295 | 
296 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
297 |         if (var != null) {
298 |           // Only process global functions.
299 |           if (var.isGlobal()) {
300 |             if (var.getInitialValue() != null &&
301 |                 var.getInitialValue().isFunction()) {
302 |               if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
303 |                 if (!processGlobalFunctionDeclaration(t, n, var)) {
304 |                   addGlobalUseOfSymbol(name, t.getModule(), VAR);
305 |                 }
306 |               } else {
307 |                 addSymbolUse(name, t.getModule(), VAR);
308 |               }
309 |             }
310 | 
311 |           // If it is not a global, it might be accessing a local of the outer
312 |           // scope. If that's the case the functions between the variable's
313 |           // declaring scope and the variable reference scope cannot be moved.
314 |           } else if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()){
315 |             for (int i = symbolStack.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
316 |               NameContext context = symbolStack.get(i);
317 |               if (context.scope == var.getScope()) {
318 |                 break;
319 |               }
320 | 
321 |               context.name.readClosureVariables = true;
322 |             }
323 |           }
324 |         }
325 |       }
326 | 
327 |       // Process prototype assignments to non-functions.
328 |       if (processNonFunctionPrototypeAssign(n, parent) != null) {
329 |         symbolStack.pop();
330 |       }
331 |     }

676 |   private List<PassFactory> getMainOptimizationLoop() {

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 830-857
Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }
837 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
838 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }
857 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.precedence(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1163-1236
Documentation:
/*
   *  0 comma ,
   *  1 assignment = += -= *= /= %= <<= >>= >>>= &= ^= |=
   *  2 conditional ?:
   *  3 logical-or ||
   *  4 logical-and &&
   *  5 bitwise-or |
   *  6 bitwise-xor ^
   *  7 bitwise-and &
   *  8 equality == !=
   *  9 relational < <= > >=
   * 10 bitwise shift << >> >>>
   * 11 addition/subtraction + -
   * 12 multiply/divide * / %
   * 13 negation/increment ! ~ - ++ --
   * 14 call, member () [] .
   */
Method code:
1163 |   static int precedence(int type) {
1164 |     switch (type) {
1165 |       case Token.COMMA:  return 0;
1166 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITOR:
1167 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR:
1168 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITAND:
1169 |       case Token.ASSIGN_LSH:
1170 |       case Token.ASSIGN_RSH:
1171 |       case Token.ASSIGN_URSH:
1172 |       case Token.ASSIGN_ADD:
1173 |       case Token.ASSIGN_SUB:
1174 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MUL:
1175 |       case Token.ASSIGN_DIV:
1176 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MOD:
1177 |       case Token.ASSIGN: return 1;
1178 |       case Token.HOOK:   return 2;  // ?: operator

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MethodCompilerPass.GatherSignatures.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MethodCompilerPass.java
Original range: 182-226
Documentation:

Method code:
182 |     @Override
183 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
184 |       switch (n.getType()) {
185 |         case Token.GETPROP:
186 |         case Token.GETELEM:
187 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
188 | 
189 |           if (dest.isString()) {
190 |             if (dest.getString().equals("prototype")) {
191 |               processPrototypeParent(t, parent);
192 |             } else {
193 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = function() {} or
194 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = baz (where baz is a
195 |               // function name). Parse tree looks like:
196 |               // assign                 <- parent
197 |               //      getprop           <- n
198 |               //          name Foo
199 |               //          string bar
200 |               //      function or name  <- n.getNext()
201 |               if (parent.isAssign() &&
202 |                   parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
203 |                 addPossibleSignature(dest.getString(), n.getNext(), t);
204 |               }
205 |             }
206 |           }
207 |           break;
208 | 
209 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
210 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
211 |             switch(key.getType()) {
212 |               case Token.STRING_KEY:
213 |                 addPossibleSignature(key.getString(), key.getFirstChild(), t);
214 |                 break;
215 |               case Token.SETTER_DEF:
216 |               case Token.GETTER_DEF:
217 |                 nonMethodProperties.add(key.getString());
218 |                 break;
219 |               default:
220 |                 throw new IllegalStateException(
221 |                     "unexpect OBJECTLIT key: " + key);
222 |             }
223 |           }
224 |           break;
225 |       }
226 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal,ReferenceMap)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java

Documentation:
/**
     * For all variables in this scope, see if they are only used once.
     * If it looks safe to do so, inline them.
     */
Method code:
194 |     private void doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal t, ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
195 | 
196 |       boolean maybeModifiedArguments =
197 |           maybeEscapedOrModifiedArguments(t.getScope(), referenceMap);
198 |       for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
199 |         Var v = it.next();
200 | 
201 |         ReferenceCollection referenceInfo = referenceMap.getReferences(v);
202 | 
203 |         // referenceInfo will be null if we're in constants-only mode
204 |         // and the variable is not a constant.
205 |         if (referenceInfo == null || isVarInlineForbidden(v)) {
206 |           // Never try to inline exported variables or variables that
207 |           // were not collected or variables that have already been inlined.
208 |           continue;
209 |         } else if (isInlineableDeclaredConstant(v, referenceInfo)) {
210 |           Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReferenceForConstants();
211 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
212 |           inlineDeclaredConstant(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
213 |           staleVars.add(v);
214 |         } else if (mode == Mode.CONSTANTS_ONLY) {
215 |           // If we're in constants-only mode, don't run more aggressive
216 |           // inlining heuristics. See InlineConstantsTest.
217 |           continue;
218 |         } else {
219 |           inlineNonConstants(v, referenceInfo, maybeModifiedArguments);
220 |         }
221 |       }
222 |     }

   * Regenerates the provides/requires if we need to do so.

205 |   private void regenerateDependencyInfoIfNecessary() throws IOException {
206 |     // If the code is NOT a JsAst, then it was not originally JS code.
207 |     // Look at the Ast for dependency info.
208 |     if (!(ast instanceof JsAst)) {
209 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(compiler,
210 |           "Expected setCompiler to be called first");
211 |       DepsFinder finder = new DepsFinder();
212 |       Node root = getAstRoot(compiler);
213 |       if (root == null) {
214 |         return;
215 |       }
216 | 
217 |       finder.visitTree(getAstRoot(compiler));
218 | 
219 |       // TODO(nicksantos|user): This caching behavior is a bit
220 |       // odd, and only works if you assume the exact call flow that

223 |       // AST, and then call getProvides() again.
224 |       //
225 |       // This won't work for any other call flow, or any sort of incremental

228 |       // multiple-scan strategy.
229 |

236 |         // getPathRelativeToClosureBase() here because we're not using
237 |         // this to generate deps files. (We're only using it for
238 |         // symbol dependencies.)

241 |             .setIncludeGoogBase(true)
242 |             .parseFile(getName(), getName(), getCode());
243 |

/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of

/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
640 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
641 |       Preconditions.checkState(
642 |           functionBody.getParent().isFunction());
643 |       Node previous = null;
644 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
645 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
646 |       // are already in the right place.
647 |       while (current != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
648 |         previous = current;
649 |         current = current.getNext();
650 |       }
651 | 
652 |       // Find any remaining declarations and move them.
653 |       Node insertAfter = previous;
654 |       while (current != null) {
655 |         // Save off the next node as the current node maybe removed.
656 |         Node next = current.getNext();
657 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
658 |           // Remove the declaration from the body.
659 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(previous);
660 |           functionBody.removeChildAfter(previous);
661 | 
662 |           // Readd the function at the top of the function body (after any
663 |           // previous declarations).
664 |           insertAfter = addToFront(functionBody, current, insertAfter);
665 |           reportCodeChange("Move function declaration not at top of function");
666 |         } else {
667 |           // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
668 |           previous = current;
669 |         }
670 |         current = next;
671 |       }
672 |     }
