===== M0509 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 121-212
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
122 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
123 |     // just bail out early here.
124 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
125 |       return this;
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
129 | 
130 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
131 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
132 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
133 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
134 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
135 |     }
136 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
137 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
138 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
139 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
140 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
141 |         }
142 |       } else {
143 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
144 |           return this;
145 |         }
146 | 
147 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
148 |         // own bizarro sub-lattice. See the commants on
149 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
150 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
151 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
152 |           FunctionType other =
153 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
154 |           FunctionType supremum =
155 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
156 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
157 |           result = null;
158 |           return this;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
162 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
163 |         // one another.
164 |         int currentIndex = 0;
165 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
166 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType()) {
176 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
177 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
178 |               return this;
179 |             }
180 |           } else {
181 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
182 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
183 |               return this;
184 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
185 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
186 |               it.remove();
187 | 
188 |               if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
189 |                 functionTypePosition = -1;
190 |               } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
191 |                 functionTypePosition--;
192 |                 currentIndex--;
193 |               }
194 |             }
195 |           }
196 |           currentIndex++;
197 |         }
198 | 
199 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
200 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
201 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
202 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
203 |         }
204 | 
205 |         alternates.add(alternate);
206 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
207 |       }
208 |     } else {
209 |       result = null;
210 |     }
211 |     return this;
212 |   }

===== M0524 =====

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 46-83

Method code:
46 |   private static boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (!block.isBlock()) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!c.isExprResult() && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:
69 |       case Token.THROW:
70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;
83 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 324-384
Documentation:

Method code:
324 |   @Override
325 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
326 |     assignmentLog = new StringBuilder();
327 | 
328 |     // Do variable reference counting.
329 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, externs, new ProcessVars(true));
330 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, new ProcessVars(false));
331 | 
332 |     // Make sure that new names don't overlap with extern names.
333 |     reservedNames.addAll(externNames);
334 | 
335 |     // Rename vars, sorted by frequency of occurrence to minimize code size.
336 |     SortedSet<Assignment> varsByFrequency =
337 |         new TreeSet<Assignment>(FREQUENCY_COMPARATOR);
338 |     varsByFrequency.addAll(assignments.values());
339 | 
340 |     if (shouldShadow) {
341 |       new ShadowVariables(
342 |           compiler, assignments, varsByFrequency, pseudoNameMap).process(
343 |               externs, root);
344 |     }
345 | 
346 |     // First try to reuse names from an earlier compilation.
347 |     if (prevUsedRenameMap != null) {
348 |       reusePreviouslyUsedVariableMap();
349 |     }
350 | 
351 |     // Assign names, sorted by descending frequency to minimize code size.
352 |     assignNames(varsByFrequency);
353 | 
354 |     boolean changed = false;
355 | 
356 |     // Rename the globals!
357 |     for (Node n : globalNameNodes) {
358 |       String newName = getNewGlobalName(n);
359 |       // Note: if newName is null, then oldName is an extern.
360 |       if (newName != null) {
361 |         n.setString(newName);
362 |         changed = true;
363 |       }
364 |     }
365 | 
366 |     // Rename the locals!
367 |     int count = 0;
368 |     for (Node n : localNameNodes) {
369 |       String newName = getNewLocalName(n);
370 |       if (newName != null) {
371 |         n.setString(newName);
372 |         changed = true;
373 |       }
374 |       count++;
375 |     }
376 | 
377 |     if (changed) {
378 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
379 |     }
380 | 
381 |     // Lastly, write the name assignments to the debug log.
382 |     compiler.addToDebugLog("JS var assignments:\n" + assignmentLog);
383 |     assignmentLog = null;
384 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.JsFileParser.parseLine(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/JsFileParser.java
Original range: 137-188
Documentation:
/**
   * Parses a line of javascript, extracting goog.provide and goog.require
   * information.
   */
Method code:
137 |   @Override
138 |   protected boolean parseLine(String line) throws ParseException {
139 |     boolean lineHasProvidesOrRequires = false;
140 | 
141 |     // Quick sanity check that will catch most cases. This is a performance
142 |     // win for people with a lot of JS.
143 |     if (line.indexOf("provide") != -1 ||
144 |         line.indexOf("require") != -1 ||
145 |         line.indexOf("addDependency") != -1) {
146 |       // Iterate over the provides/requires.
147 |       googMatcher.reset(line);
148 |       while (googMatcher.find()) {
149 |         lineHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
150 | 
151 |         if (includeGoogBase && !fileHasProvidesOrRequires) {
152 |           fileHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
153 |           requires.add("goog");
154 |         }
155 | 
156 |         // See if it's a require or provide.
157 |         char firstChar = googMatcher.group(1).charAt(0);
158 |         boolean isProvide = firstChar == 'p';
159 |         boolean isRequire = firstChar == 'r';
160 | 
161 |         if (isProvide || isRequire) {
162 |           // Parse the param.
163 |           String arg = parseJsString(googMatcher.group(2));
164 | 
165 |           // Add the dependency.
166 |           if (isRequire) {
167 |             // goog is always implicit.
168 |             // TODO(nicksantos): I'm pretty sure we don't need this anymore.
169 |             // Remove this later.
170 |             if (!"goog".equals(arg)) {
171 |               requires.add(arg);
172 |             }
173 |           } else {
174 |             provides.add(arg);
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 |     } else if (includeGoogBase && line.startsWith(BASE_JS_START) &&
179 |                provides.isEmpty() && requires.isEmpty()) {
180 |       provides.add("goog");
181 | 
182 |       // base.js can't provide or require anything else.
183 |       return false;
184 |     }
185 | 
186 |     return !shortcutMode || lineHasProvidesOrRequires ||
187 |         CharMatcher.WHITESPACE.matchesAllOf(line);
188 |   }

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1195 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1196 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {
1197 |       return -1;
1198 |     } else if ((charno & ~COLUMN_MASK) != 0) {
1199 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1200 |     } else {
1201 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | (charno & COLUMN_MASK);
1202 |     }
1203 |   }

92 |         ReferenceCollection referenceInfo = referenceMap.getReferences(v);
93 | 
94 |         if (isInlinableObject(referenceInfo.references)) {
95 |           // Blacklist the object itself, as well as any other values
96 |           // that it refers to, since they will have been moved around.
97 |           staleVars.add(v);
98 | 
99 |           Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
100 |           Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
101 | 
102 |           // Split up the object into individual variables if the object
103 |           // is never referenced directly in full.
104 |           splitObject(v, declaration, init, referenceInfo);
105 |         }
106 |       }
107 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java
Original range: 341-367
Documentation:

Method code:
341 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
342 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
343 |     // two cases:
344 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
345 |     // and
346 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
347 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
348 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
349 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
350 |     //
351 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
352 |     //
353 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
354 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
355 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
356 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
357 |     //
358 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
359 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
360 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
361 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
362 | 
363 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
364 |           registry, this.getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
365 |     }
366 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);
367 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceIf(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 297-368
Documentation:
/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
297 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
298 | 
299 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
300 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
301 |       if (child.isIf()){
302 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
303 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
304 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
305 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
306 | 
307 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null
308 |             && isReturnBlock(thenBranch)
309 |             && nextNode.isIf()) {
310 |           Node nextCond = nextNode.getFirstChild();
311 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
312 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
313 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
314 |             // Transform
315 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
316 |             // to
317 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
318 |             child.detachFromParent();
319 |             child.detachChildren();
320 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
321 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
322 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
323 |             reportCodeChange();
324 |           } else if (nextElse != null
325 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
326 |             // Transform
327 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
328 |             // to
329 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
330 |             child.detachFromParent();
331 |             child.detachChildren();
332 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
333 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
334 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
335 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
336 |             reportCodeChange();
337 |           }
338 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
339 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
340 |           Node thenExpr = null;
341 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
342 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
343 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
344 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
345 |           } else {
346 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
347 |           }
348 | 
349 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
350 | 
351 |           cond.detachFromParent();
352 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
353 | 
354 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
355 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
356 |                                     .srcref(child));
357 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
358 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
359 |           reportCodeChange();
360 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
361 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
362 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
363 |           reportCodeChange();
364 |         }
365 |       }
366 |     }
367 |     return n;
368 |   }

   * Given an entry node, find all the nodes reachable from that node

196 |   private void prioritizeFromEntryNode(DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry) {
197 |     PriorityQueue<DiGraphNode<Node, Branch>> worklist =

===== M0588 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 508-530
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An rvalue in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
508 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
509 |       switch (n.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
511 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
512 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
513 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
514 |         case Token.OR:
515 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
516 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
517 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
518 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
519 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
520 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
521 |         case Token.HOOK:
522 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
523 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
524 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
525 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
526 |           Node third = second.getNext();
527 |           return getValueType(third);
528 |       }
529 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
530 |     }

===== M0604 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 606-658
Documentation:

Method code:
606 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
607 |   static <T> T runCallable(
608 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
609 | 
610 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
611 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
612 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
613 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
614 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
615 | 
616 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
617 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
618 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
619 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
620 |       @Override
621 |       public void run() {
622 |         try {
623 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
624 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
625 |           }
626 |           result[0] = callable.call();
627 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
628 |           exception[0] = e;
629 |         } finally {
630 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
631 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
632 |           }
633 |         }
634 |       }
635 |     };
636 | 
637 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
638 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
639 |       th.start();
640 |       while (true) {
641 |         try {
642 |           th.join();
643 |           break;
644 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
645 |           // ignore
646 |         }
647 |       }
648 |     } else {
649 |       runnable.run();
650 |     }
651 | 
652 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
653 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
654 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
655 |     }
656 | 
657 |     return (T) result[0];
658 |   }

/**
   * Creates name information for the current node during a traversal.
   *

   * @return The name information, or null if the name is irrelevant to this

Method code:
1318 |   private NameInformation createNameInformation(NodeTraversal t, Node n,
1319 |       Node parent) {
1320 |     // Build the full name and find its root node by iterating down through all
1321 |     // GETPROP/GETELEM nodes.
1322 |     String name = "";
1323 |     Node rootNameNode = n;
1324 |     boolean bNameWasShortened = false;
1325 |     while (true) {
1326 |       if (NodeUtil.isGet(rootNameNode)) {
1327 |         Node prop = rootNameNode.getLastChild();
1328 |         if (rootNameNode.isGetProp()) {
1329 |           name = "." + prop.getString() + name;
1330 |         } else {
1331 |           // We consider the name to be "a.b" in a.b['c'] or a.b[x].d.
1332 |           bNameWasShortened = true;
1333 |           name = "";
1334 |         }
1335 |         rootNameNode = rootNameNode.getFirstChild();
1336 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(
1337 |           rootNameNode, rootNameNode.getParent())) {
1338 |         name = "." + rootNameNode.getString() + name;
1339 | 
1340 |         // Check if this is an object literal assigned to something.
1341 |         Node objLit = rootNameNode.getParent();
1342 |         Node objLitParent = objLit.getParent();
1343 |         if (objLitParent.isAssign()) {
1344 |           // This must be the right side of the assign.
1345 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent.getFirstChild();
1346 |         } else if (objLitParent.isName()) {
1347 |           // This must be a VAR initialization.
1348 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent;
1349 |         } else if (objLitParent.isStringKey()) {
1350 |           // This must be a object literal key initialization.
1351 |           rootNameNode = objLitParent;
1352 |         } else {
1353 |           return null;
1354 |         }
1355 |       } else {
1356 |         break;
1357 |       }
1358 |     }
1359 | 
1360 |     // Check whether this is a class-defining call. Classes may only be defined
1361 |     // in the global scope.
1362 |     if (parent.isCall() && t.inGlobalScope()) {
1363 |       CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
1364 |       SubclassRelationship classes = convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(parent);
1365 |       if (classes != null) {
1366 |         NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1367 |         nameInfo.name = classes.subclassName;
1368 |         nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef = true;
1369 |         nameInfo.superclass = classes.superclassName;
1370 |         return nameInfo;
1371 |       }
1372 | 
1373 |       String singletonGetterClass =
1374 |           convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(parent);
1375 |       if (singletonGetterClass != null) {
1376 |         NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1377 |         nameInfo.name = singletonGetterClass;
1378 |         nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef = true;
1379 |         return nameInfo;
1380 |       }
1381 |     }
1382 | 
1383 |     switch (rootNameNode.getType()) {
1384 |       case Token.NAME:
1385 |         // Check whether this is an assignment to a prototype property
1386 |         // of an object defined in the global scope.
1387 |         if (!bNameWasShortened &&
1388 |             n.isGetProp() &&
1389 |             parent.isAssign() &&
1390 |             "prototype".equals(n.getLastChild().getString())) {
1391 |           if (createNameInformation(t, n.getFirstChild(), n) != null) {
1392 |             name = rootNameNode.getString() + name;
1393 |             name = name.substring(0, name.length() - PROTOTYPE_SUFFIX_LEN);
1394 |             NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1395 |             nameInfo.name = name;
1396 |             return nameInfo;
1397 |           } else {
1398 |             return null;
1399 |           }
1400 |         }

1402 |             rootNameNode.getString() + name, t.getScope(), rootNameNode);
1403 |       case Token.THIS:
1404 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
1405 |           NameInformation nameInfo = new NameInformation();
1406 |           if (name.indexOf('.') == 0) {

1408 |           } else {

1410 |           }

1415 |       default:

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.removeChild(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1751-1804
Documentation:
/** Safely remove children while maintaining a valid node structure. */
Method code:
1751 |   static void removeChild(Node parent, Node node) {
1752 |     if (isTryFinallyNode(parent, node)) {
1753 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(getCatchBlock(parent))) {
1754 |         // A finally can only be removed if there is a catch.
1755 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1756 |       } else {
1757 |         // Otherwise only its children can be removed.
1758 |         node.detachChildren();
1759 |       }
1760 |     } else if (node.isCatch()) {
1761 |       // The CATCH can can only be removed if there is a finally clause.
1762 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent().getParent();
1763 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1764 |       node.detachFromParent();
1765 |     } else if (isTryCatchNodeContainer(node)) {
1766 |       // The container node itself can't be removed, but the contained CATCH
1767 |       // can if there is a 'finally' clause
1768 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent();
1769 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1770 |       node.detachChildren();
1771 |     } else if (node.isBlock()) {
1772 |       // Simply empty the block.  This maintains source location and
1773 |       // "synthetic"-ness.
1774 |       node.detachChildren();
1775 |     } else if (isStatementBlock(parent)
1776 |         || isSwitchCase(node)) {
1777 |       // A statement in a block can simply be removed.
1778 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1779 |     } else if (parent.isVar()) {
1780 |       if (parent.hasMoreThanOneChild()) {
1781 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1782 |       } else {
1783 |         // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1784 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1785 |         // This would leave an empty VAR, remove the VAR itself.
1786 |         removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1787 |       }
1788 |     } else if (parent.isLabel()
1789 |         && node == parent.getLastChild()) {
1790 |       // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1791 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1792 |       // A LABEL without children can not be referred to, remove it.
1793 |       removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1794 |     } else if (parent.isFor()
1795 |         && parent.getChildCount() == 4) {
1796 |       // Only Token.FOR can have an Token.EMPTY other control structure
1797 |       // need something for the condition. Others need to be replaced
1798 |       // or the structure removed.
1799 |       parent.replaceChild(node, IR.empty());
1800 |     } else {
1801 |       throw new IllegalStateException("Invalid attempt to remove node: " +
1802 |           node.toString() + " of "+ parent.toString());
1803 |     }
1804 |   }

===== M0624 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DevirtualizePrototypeMethods.isEligibleDefinition(SimpleDefinitionFinder,DefinitionSite)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DevirtualizePrototypeMethods.java
Original range: 239-312
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if a method definition is eligible for rewrite as a
   * global function.  In order to be eligible for rewrite, the
   * definition must:
   *
   * - Refer to a function that takes a fixed number of arguments.
   * - Function must not be exported.
   * - Function must be used at least once.
   * - Property is never accessed outside a function call context.
   * - The definition under consideration must be the only possible
   *   choice at each call site.
   * - Definition must happen in a module loaded before the first use.
   */
Method code:
239 |   private boolean isEligibleDefinition(SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder,
240 |                                        DefinitionSite definitionSite) {
241 | 
242 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
243 |     JSModule definitionModule = definitionSite.module;
244 | 
245 |     // Only functions may be rewritten.
246 |     // Functions that access "arguments" are not eligible since
247 |     // rewrite changes the structure of this object.
248 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
249 |     if (rValue == null ||
250 |         !rValue.isFunction() ||
251 |         NodeUtil.isVarArgsFunction(rValue)) {
252 |       return false;
253 |     }
254 | 
255 |     // Exporting a method prevents rewrite.
256 |     Node lValue = definition.getLValue();
257 |     if ((lValue == null) ||
258 |         !lValue.isGetProp()) {
259 |       return false;
260 |     }
261 |     CodingConvention codingConvention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
262 |     if (codingConvention.isExported(lValue.getLastChild().getString())) {
263 |       return false;
264 |     }
265 | 
266 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
267 | 
268 |     // Rewriting unused methods is not sound.
269 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
270 |       return false;
271 |     }
272 | 
273 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
274 | 
275 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
276 |       // Accessing the property directly prevents rewrite.
277 |       if (!isCall(site)) {
278 |         return false;
279 |       }
280 | 
281 |       Node nameNode = site.node;
282 | 
283 |       // Don't rewrite methods called in functions that can't be specialized
284 |       // if we are specializing
285 |       if (specializationState != null &&
286 |           !specializationState.canFixupSpecializedFunctionContainingNode(
287 |               nameNode)) {
288 |         return false;
289 |       }
290 | 
291 |       // Multiple definitions prevent rewrite.
292 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
293 |           defFinder.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
294 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
295 |         return false;
296 |       }
297 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
298 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
299 | 
300 |       // Accessing the property in a module loaded before the
301 |       // definition module prevents rewrite; accessing a variable
302 |       // before definition results in a parse error.
303 |       JSModule callModule = site.module;
304 |       if ((definitionModule != callModule) &&
305 |           ((callModule == null) ||
306 |           !moduleGraph.dependsOn(callModule, definitionModule))) {
307 |         return false;
308 |       }
309 |     }
310 | 
311 |     return true;
312 |   }

===== M0643 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GoogleCodingConvention.isConstant(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GoogleCodingConvention.java
Original range: 70-87
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
70 |   @Override
71 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
72 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
73 |       return false;
74 |     }
75 | 
76 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
77 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
78 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
79 |     if (pos >= 0) {
80 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
81 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
82 |         return false;
83 |       }
84 |     }
85 | 
86 |     return isConstantKey(name);
87 |   }

/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgement.
     */
Method code:

311 |       int size = references.size();
312 |       if (size == 0) {
313 |         return false;
314 |       }
315 | 
316 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
317 |       // it's not well-defined.
318 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
319 |       if (init == null) {
320 |         return false;
321 |       }
322 | 
323 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
324 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
325 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
326 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
327 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
328 |           return false;
329 |         }
330 |       }
331 | 
332 |       return true;
333 |     }

===== M0663 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 560-607
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
560 |     private void extractForInitializer(
561 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
562 | 
563 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
564 |         next = c.getNext();
565 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
566 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
567 |         switch (c.getType()) {
568 |           case Token.LABEL:
569 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
570 |             break;
571 |           case Token.FOR:
572 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
573 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
574 |               if (first.isVar()) {
575 |                 // Transform:
576 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
577 |                 // to:
578 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
579 |                 Node newStatement = first;
580 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
581 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
582 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
583 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
584 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
585 |               }
586 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
587 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
588 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
589 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
590 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
591 | 
592 |               Node newStatement;
593 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
594 |               // but are handled differently.
595 |               if (init.isVar()) {
596 |                 newStatement = init;
597 |               } else {
598 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
599 |               }
600 | 
601 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
602 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
603 |             }
604 |             break;
605 |         }
606 |       }
607 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PureFunctionIdentifier.markPureFunctionCalls()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PureFunctionIdentifier.java
Original range: 307-365
Documentation:
/**
   * Set no side effect property at pure-function call sites.
   */
Method code:
307 |   private void markPureFunctionCalls() {
308 |     for (Node callNode : allFunctionCalls) {
309 |       Node name = callNode.getFirstChild();
310 |       Collection<Definition> defs =
311 |           getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider, name);
312 |       // Default to side effects, non-local results
313 |       Node.SideEffectFlags flags = new Node.SideEffectFlags();
314 |       if (defs == null) {
315 |         flags.setMutatesGlobalState();
316 |         flags.setThrows();
317 |         flags.setReturnsTainted();
318 |       } else {
319 |         flags.clearAllFlags();
320 |         for (Definition def : defs) {
321 |           FunctionInformation functionInfo =
322 |               functionSideEffectMap.get(def.getRValue());
323 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(functionInfo);
324 |           // TODO(johnlenz): set the arguments separately from the
325 |           // global state flag.
326 |           if (functionInfo.mutatesGlobalState()) {
327 |             flags.setMutatesGlobalState();
328 |           }
329 | 
330 |           if (functionInfo.functionThrows) {
331 |             flags.setThrows();
332 |           }
333 | 
334 |           if (!callNode.isNew()) {
335 |             if (functionInfo.taintsThis) {
336 |               flags.setMutatesThis();
337 |             }
338 |           }
339 | 
340 |           if (functionInfo.taintsReturn) {
341 |             flags.setReturnsTainted();
342 |           }
343 | 
344 |           if (flags.areAllFlagsSet()) {
345 |             break;
346 |           }
347 |         }
348 |       }
349 | 
350 |       // Handle special cases (Math, RegEx)
351 |       if (callNode.isCall()) {
352 |         Preconditions.checkState(compiler != null);
353 |         if (!NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects(callNode, compiler)) {
354 |           flags.clearSideEffectFlags();
355 |         }
356 |       } else if (callNode.isNew()) {
357 |         // Handle known cases now (Object, Date, RegExp, etc)
358 |         if (!NodeUtil.constructorCallHasSideEffects(callNode)) {
359 |           flags.clearSideEffectFlags();
360 |         }
361 |       }
362 | 
363 |       callNode.setSideEffectFlags(flags.valueOf());
364 |     }
365 |   }

===== M0671 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.add(Node,Context)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 85-732
Documentation:

Method code:
85 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
86 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
87 |       return;
88 |     }
89 | 
90 |     int type = n.getType();
91 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
92 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
93 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
94 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
95 | 
96 |     // Handle all binary operators
97 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
98 |       Preconditions.checkState(
99 |           childCount == 2,
100 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
101 |           opstr, childCount);
102 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
103 | 
104 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
105 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
106 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
107 | 
108 |       // Handle associativity.
109 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
110 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.
111 |       if (last.getType() == type &&
112 |           NodeUtil.isAssociative(type)) {
113 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
114 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
115 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
116 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
117 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
118 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
119 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
120 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
121 |       } else {
122 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, type, opstr, context, rhsContext, p, p + 1);
123 |       }
124 |       return;
125 |     }
126 | 
127 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);
128 | 
129 |     switch (type) {
130 |       case Token.TRY: {
131 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getNext().isBlock() &&
132 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());
133 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount >= 2 && childCount <= 3);
134 | 
135 |         add("try");
136 |         add(first, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
137 | 
138 |         // second child contains the catch block, or nothing if there
139 |         // isn't a catch block
140 |         Node catchblock = first.getNext().getFirstChild();
141 |         if (catchblock != null) {
142 |           add(catchblock);
143 |         }
144 | 
145 |         if (childCount == 3) {
146 |           add("finally");
147 |           add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
148 |         }
149 |         break;
150 |       }
151 | 
152 |       case Token.CATCH:
153 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
154 |         add("catch(");
155 |         add(first);
156 |         add(")");
157 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
158 |         break;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.THROW:
161 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
162 |         add("throw");
163 |         add(first);
164 | 
165 |         // Must have a ';' after a throw statement, otherwise safari can't
166 |         // parse this.
167 |         cc.endStatement(true);
168 |         break;
169 | 
170 |       case Token.RETURN:
171 |         add("return");
172 |         if (childCount == 1) {
173 |           add(first);
174 |         } else {
175 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
176 |         }
177 |         cc.endStatement();
178 |         break;
179 | 
180 |       case Token.VAR:
181 |         if (first != null) {
182 |           add("var ");
183 |           addList(first, false, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
184 |         }
185 |         break;
186 | 
187 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
188 |         Preconditions.checkState(!n.getString().isEmpty());
189 |         addIdentifier(n.getString());
190 |         break;
191 | 
192 |       case Token.NAME:
193 |         if (first == null || first.isEmpty()) {
194 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
195 |         } else {
196 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
197 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
198 |           cc.addOp("=", true);
199 |           if (first.isComma()) {
200 |             addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.ASSIGN), Context.OTHER);
201 |           } else {
202 |             // Add expression, consider nearby code at lowest level of
203 |             // precedence.
204 |             addExpr(first, 0, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
205 |           }
206 |         }
207 |         break;
208 | 
209 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
210 |         add("[");
211 |         addArrayList(first);
212 |         add("]");
213 |         break;
214 | 
215 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
216 |         add("(");
217 |         addList(first);
218 |         add(")");
219 |         break;
220 | 
221 |       case Token.COMMA:
222 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
223 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, Token.COMMA, ",", context, Context.OTHER, 0, 0);
224 |         break;
225 | 
226 |       case Token.NUMBER:
227 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
228 |         cc.addNumber(n.getDouble());
229 |         break;
230 | 
231 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
232 |       case Token.VOID:
233 |       case Token.NOT:
234 |       case Token.BITNOT:
235 |       case Token.POS: {
236 |         // All of these unary operators are right-associative
237 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
238 |         cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
239 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
240 |         break;
241 |       }
242 | 
243 |       case Token.NEG: {
244 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
245 | 
246 |         // It's important to our sanity checker that the code
247 |         // we print produces the same AST as the code we parse back.
248 |         // NEG is a weird case because Rhino parses "- -2" as "2".
249 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isNumber()) {
250 |           cc.addNumber(-n.getFirstChild().getDouble());
251 |         } else {
252 |           cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
253 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
254 |         }
255 | 
256 |         break;
257 |       }
258 | 
259 |       case Token.HOOK: {
260 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
261 |         int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
262 |         addExpr(first, p + 1, context);
263 |         cc.addOp("?", true);
264 |         addExpr(first.getNext(), 1, Context.OTHER);
265 |         cc.addOp(":", true);
266 |         addExpr(last, 1, Context.OTHER);
267 |         break;
268 |       }
269 | 
270 |       case Token.REGEXP:
271 |         if (!first.isString() ||
272 |             !last.isString()) {
273 |           throw new Error("Expected children to be strings");
274 |         }
275 | 
276 |         String regexp = regexpEscape(first.getString(), outputCharsetEncoder);
277 | 
278 |         // I only use one .add because whitespace matters
279 |         if (childCount == 2) {
280 |           add(regexp + last.getString());
281 |         } else {
282 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
283 |           add(regexp);
284 |         }
285 |         break;
286 | 
287 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
288 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
289 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
290 |         }
291 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
292 |         boolean funcNeedsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
293 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
294 |           add("(");
295 |         }
296 | 
297 |         add("function");
298 |         add(first);
299 | 
300 |         add(first.getNext());
301 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
302 |         cc.endFunction(context == Context.STATEMENT);
303 | 
304 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
305 |           add(")");
306 |         }

309 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:

315 |         // Get methods are unnamed

319 |           Preconditions.checkState(!first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasChildren());
320 |           add("get ");
321 |         } else {
322 |           // Set methods have one parameter.
323 |           Preconditions.checkState(first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasOneChild());

390 |         }

392 |       }

404 |           add(";");

408 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
409 |         } else {

411 |           add("for(");
412 |           add(first);

415 |           add(")");

418 |         }
419 |         break;
420 |

423 |         add("do");

425 |         add("while(");
426 |         add(last);
427 |         add(")");
428 |         cc.endStatement();
429 |         break;
430 |

432 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
433 |         add("while(");
434 |         add(first);
435 |         add(")");
436 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
437 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
438 |         break;

442 |         break;
443 |

466 |             childCount == 2,

469 |         add("[");

471 |         add("]");
472 |         break;

476 |         add("with(");

489 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.

503 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
504 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
505 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
506 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,

515 |         } else {

517 |         }

521 |         break;

548 |         }

553 |         add("null");

===== M0674 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 586-623
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured vairables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
586 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
587 |     switch (n.getType()) {
588 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
589 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
590 |              child = child.getNext()) {
591 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
592 |             return false;
593 |           }
594 |         }
595 |         return true;
596 | 
597 |       case Token.REGEXP:
598 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
599 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
600 |              child = child.getNext()) {
601 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
602 |             return false;
603 |           }
604 |         }
605 |         return true;
606 | 
607 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
608 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
609 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
610 |              child = child.getNext()) {
611 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
612 |             return false;
613 |           }
614 |         }
615 |         return true;
616 | 
617 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
618 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
619 | 
620 |       default:
621 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
622 |     }
623 |   }

===== M0679 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.referenceAliases()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1270-1279
Documentation:
/**
   * The NameAnalyzer algorithm works best when all objects have a canonical
   * name in the global scope. When multiple names in the global scope
   * point to the same object, things start to break down.
   *
   * For example, if we have
   * <code>
   * var a = {};
   * var b = a;
   * a.foo = 3;
   * alert(b.foo);
   * </code>
   * then a.foo and b.foo are the same name, even though NameAnalyzer doesn't
   * represent them as such.
   *
   * To handle this case, we look at all the aliases in the program.
   * If descendant properties of that alias are assigned, then we create a
   * directional reference from the original name to the alias. For example,
   * in this case, the assign to {@code a.foo} triggers a reference from
   * {@code b} to {@code a}, but NOT from a to b.
   *
   * Similarly, "instanceof" checks do not prevent the removal
   * of a unaliased name but an instanceof check on an alias can only be removed
   * if the other aliases are also removed, so we add a connection here.
   */
Method code:
1270 |   private void referenceAliases() {
1271 |     for (Map.Entry<String, AliasSet> entry : aliases.entrySet()) {
1272 |       JsName name = getName(entry.getKey(), false);
1273 |       if (name.hasWrittenDescendants || name.hasInstanceOfReference) {
1274 |         for (String alias : entry.getValue().names) {
1275 |           recordReference(alias, entry.getKey(), RefType.REGULAR);
1276 |         }
1277 |       }
1278 |     }
1279 |   }

85 |     // then dispatch to specific folding method.
86 |     Node callTarget = subtree.getFirstChild();

88 |       return subtree;
89 |     }

92 |       return subtree;

95 |     Node stringNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();

98 |     if ((!stringNode.isString()) ||

111 |         subtree = tryFoldStringToUpperCase(subtree, stringNode);

121 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("substring")) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.collapseAssignEqualTo(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 108-199
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse the given assign expression into the expression directly
   * following it, if possible.
   *
   * @param expr The expression that may be moved.
   * @param exprParent The parent of {@code expr}.
   * @param value The value of this expression, expressed as a node. Each
   *     expression may have multiple values, so this function may be called
   *     multiple times for the same expression. For example,
   *     <code>
   *     a = true;
   *     </code>
   *     is equal to the name "a" and the boolean "true".
   * @return Whether the expression was collapsed succesfully.
   */
Method code:
108 |   private boolean collapseAssignEqualTo(Node expr, Node exprParent,
109 |       Node value) {
110 |     Node assign = expr.getFirstChild();
111 |     Node parent = exprParent;
112 |     Node next = expr.getNext();
113 |     while (next != null) {
114 |       switch (next.getType()) {
115 |         case Token.AND:
116 |         case Token.OR:
117 |         case Token.HOOK:
118 |         case Token.IF:
119 |         case Token.RETURN:
120 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
121 |           // Dive down the left side
122 |           parent = next;
123 |           next = next.getFirstChild();
124 |           break;
125 | 
126 |         case Token.VAR:
127 |           if (next.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
128 |             parent = next.getFirstChild();
129 |             next = parent.getFirstChild();
130 |             break;
131 |           }
132 |           return false;
133 | 
134 |         case Token.GETPROP:
135 |         case Token.NAME:
136 |           if (next.isQualifiedName()) {
137 |             String nextName = next.getQualifiedName();
138 |             if (value.isQualifiedName() &&
139 |                 nextName.equals(value.getQualifiedName())) {
140 |               // If the previous expression evaluates to value of a
141 |               // qualified name, and that qualified name is used again
142 |               // shortly, then we can exploit the assign here.
143 | 
144 |               // Verify the assignment doesn't change its own value.
145 |               if (!isSafeReplacement(next, assign)) {
146 |                 return false;
147 |               }
148 | 
149 |               exprParent.removeChild(expr);
150 |               expr.removeChild(assign);
151 |               parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
152 |               return true;
153 |             }
154 |           }
155 |           return false;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
158 |           // Assigns are really tricky. In lots of cases, we want to inline
159 |           // into the right side of the assign. But the left side of the
160 |           // assign is evaluated first, and it may have convoluted logic:
161 |           //   a = null;
162 |           //   (a = b).c = null;
163 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign. Similarly:
164 |           //   a.b = null;
165 |           //   a.b.c = null;
166 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign either.
167 |           //
168 |           // To protect against this, we simply only inline when the left side
169 |           // is guaranteed to evaluate to the same L-value no matter what.
170 |           Node leftSide = next.getFirstChild();
171 |           if (leftSide.isName() ||
172 |               leftSide.isGetProp() &&
173 |               leftSide.getFirstChild().isThis()) {
174 |             // Dive down the right side of the assign.
175 |             parent = next;
176 |             next = leftSide.getNext();
177 |             break;
178 |           } else {
179 |             return false;
180 |           }
181 | 
182 |         default:
183 |           if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(next)
184 |               && next.isEquivalentTo(value)) {
185 |             // If the r-value of the expr assign is an immutable value,
186 |             // and the value is used again shortly, then we can exploit
187 |             // the assign here.
188 |             exprParent.removeChild(expr);
189 |             expr.removeChild(assign);
190 |             parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
191 |             return true;
192 |           }
193 |           // Return without inlining a thing
194 |           return false;
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 | 
198 |     return false;
199 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseProperties.inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseProperties.java
Original range: 161-197
Documentation:
/**
   * For each qualified name N in the global scope, we check if:
   * (a) No ancestor of N is ever aliased or assigned an unknown value type.
   *     (If N = "a.b.c", "a" and "a.b" are never aliased).
   * (b) N has exactly one write, and it lives in the global scope.
   * (c) N is aliased in a local scope.
   *
   * If (a) is true, then GlobalNamespace must know all the writes to N.
   * If (a) and (b) are true, then N cannot change during the execution of
   *    a local scope.
   * If (a) and (b) and (c) are true, then the alias can be inlined if the
   *    alias obeys the usual rules for how we decide whether a variable is
   *    inlineable.
   * @see InlineVariables
   */
Method code:
161 |   private void inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace namespace) {
162 |     // Invariant: All the names in the worklist meet condition (a).
163 |     Deque<Name> workList = new ArrayDeque<Name>(namespace.getNameForest());
164 |     while (!workList.isEmpty()) {
165 |       Name name = workList.pop();
166 | 
167 |       // Don't attempt to inline a getter or setter property as a variable.
168 |       if (name.type == Name.Type.GET || name.type == Name.Type.SET) {
169 |         continue;
170 |       }
171 | 
172 |       if (name.globalSets == 1 && name.localSets == 0 &&
173 |           name.aliasingGets > 0) {
174 |         // {@code name} meets condition (b). Find all of its local aliases
175 |         // and try to inline them.
176 |         List<Ref> refs = Lists.newArrayList(name.getRefs());
177 |         for (Ref ref : refs) {
178 |           if (ref.type == Type.ALIASING_GET && ref.scope.isLocal()) {
179 |             // {@code name} meets condition (c). Try to inline it.
180 |             if (inlineAliasIfPossible(ref, namespace)) {
181 |               name.removeRef(ref);
182 |             }
183 |           }
184 |         }
185 |       }
186 | 
187 |       // Check if {@code name} has any aliases left after the
188 |       // local-alias-inlining above.
189 |       if ((name.type == Name.Type.OBJECTLIT ||
190 |            name.type == Name.Type.FUNCTION) &&
191 |           name.aliasingGets == 0 && name.props != null) {
192 |         // All of {@code name}'s children meet condition (a), so they can be
193 |         // added to the worklist.
194 |         workList.addAll(name.props);
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 |   }

/**
   * Since this pass reports errors only when a global {@code this} keyword
   * is encountered, there is no reason to traverse non global contexts.
   */
Method code:
79 |   @Override
80 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
81 | 
82 |     if (n.isFunction()) {
83 |       // Don't traverse functions that are constructors or have the @this
84 |       // or @override annotation.
85 |       JSDocInfo jsDoc = getFunctionJsDocInfo(n);
86 |       if (jsDoc != null &&
87 |           (jsDoc.isConstructor() ||
88 |            jsDoc.isInterface() ||
89 |            jsDoc.hasThisType() ||
90 |            jsDoc.isOverride())) {
91 |         return false;
92 |       }
93 | 
94 |       // Don't traverse functions unless they would normally
95 |       // be able to have a @this annotation associated with them. e.g.,
96 |       // var a = function() { }; // or
97 |       // function a() {} // or
98 |       // a.x = function() {}; // or
99 |       // var a = {x: function() {}};
100 |       int pType = parent.getType();
101 |       if (!(pType == Token.BLOCK ||
102 |             pType == Token.SCRIPT ||
103 |             pType == Token.NAME ||
104 |             pType == Token.ASSIGN ||
105 | 
106 |             // object literal keys
107 |             pType == Token.STRING_KEY)) {
108 |         return false;
109 |       }
110 | 
111 |       // Don't traverse functions that are getting lent to a prototype.
112 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
113 |       if (NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(parent, gramps)) {
114 |         JSDocInfo maybeLends = gramps.getJSDocInfo();
115 |         if (maybeLends != null &&
116 |             maybeLends.getLendsName() != null &&
117 |             maybeLends.getLendsName().endsWith(".prototype")) {
118 |           return false;
119 |         }
120 |       }
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     if (parent != null && parent.isAssign()) {
124 |       Node lhs = parent.getFirstChild();
125 |       Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
126 | 
127 |       if (n == lhs) {
128 |         // Always traverse the left side of the assignment. To handle
129 |         // nested assignments properly (e.g., (a = this).property = c;),
130 |         // assignLhsChild should not be overridden.
131 |         if (assignLhsChild == null) {
132 |           assignLhsChild = lhs;
133 |         }
134 |       } else {
135 |         // Only traverse the right side if it's not an assignment to a prototype
136 |         // property or subproperty.
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isGet(lhs)) {
138 |           if (lhs.isGetProp() &&
139 |               lhs.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
140 |             return false;
141 |           }
142 |           Node llhs = lhs.getFirstChild();
143 |           if (llhs.isGetProp() &&
144 |               llhs.getLastChild().getString().equals("prototype")) {
145 |             return false;
146 |           }
147 |         }
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     return true;
152 |   }

/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.

890 |     void replace() {
891 |       if (firstNode == null) {
892 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
893 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
894 |         return;
895 |       }
896 | 
897 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
898 |       // provided symbol.
899 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
900 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
901 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
902 | 
903 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
904 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
905 |         if (candidateDefinition.isExprResult() &&
906 |             !candidateDefinition.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {
907 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);

909 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
910 |           if (nameNode.isName()) {
911 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
912 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
913 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
914 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
915 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);

920 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
921 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();

923 |           }
924 |         }
925 |       } else {
926 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
927 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
928 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
929 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
930 |         } else {

932 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.

936 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)

940 |             ProvidedName parentName =

942 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 124-170

/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
124 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.STRING:
127 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
128 | 
129 |       case Token.NUMBER:
130 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
131 | 
132 |       case Token.NOT:
133 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
134 | 
135 |       case Token.NULL:
136 |       case Token.FALSE:
137 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
138 | 
139 |       case Token.VOID:
140 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
141 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
142 |         }
143 |         break;
144 | 
145 |       case Token.NAME:
146 |         String name = n.getString();
147 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
148 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
149 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
150 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
151 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
152 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
153 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
154 |         }
155 |         break;
156 | 
157 |       case Token.TRUE:
158 |       case Token.REGEXP:
159 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
160 | 
161 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
162 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
163 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
164 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
165 |         }
166 |         break;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
170 |   }

Method code:
64 |   public SortedDependencies(List<INPUT> inputs)
65 |       throws CircularDependencyException {
66 |     this.inputs = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
67 |     noProvides = Lists.newArrayList();
68 | 
69 |     // Collect all symbols provided in these files.
70 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
71 |       Collection<String> currentProvides = input.getProvides();
72 |       if (currentProvides.isEmpty()) {
73 |         noProvides.add(input);
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       for (String provide : currentProvides) {
77 |         provideMap.put(provide, input);
78 |       }
79 |     }
80 | 
81 |     // Get the direct dependencies.
82 |     final Multimap<INPUT, INPUT> deps = HashMultimap.create();
83 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
84 |       for (String req : input.getRequires()) {
85 |         INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
86 |         if (dep != null && dep != input) {
87 |           deps.put(input, dep);
88 |         }
89 |       }
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     // Sort the inputs by sucking in 0-in-degree nodes until we're done.
93 |     sortedList = topologicalStableSort(inputs, deps);
94 | 
95 |     // The dependency graph of inputs has a cycle iff sortedList is a proper
96 |     // subset of inputs. Also, it has a cycle iff the subgraph
97 |     // (inputs - sortedList) has a cycle. It's fairly easy to prove this
98 |     // by the lemma that a graph has a cycle iff it has a subgraph where
99 |     // no nodes have out-degree 0. I'll leave the proof of this as an exercise
100 |     // to the reader.
101 |     if (sortedList.size() < inputs.size()) {
102 |       List<INPUT> subGraph = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
103 |       subGraph.removeAll(sortedList);
104 | 
105 |       throw new CircularDependencyException(
106 |           cycleToString(findCycle(subGraph, deps)));
107 |     }
108 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1905 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1906 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1907 |   }

Documentation:
/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
409 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
410 |       Node ret;
411 |       if (n instanceof Name) {
412 |         ret = transformNameAsString((Name)n);
413 |       } else if (n instanceof NumberLiteral) {
414 |         ret = transformNumberAsString((NumberLiteral)n);
415 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
416 |       } else {
417 |         ret = transform(n);
418 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
419 |       }
420 |       Preconditions.checkState(ret.isString());
421 |       return ret;
422 |     }

190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       Node endMarkerNode = parent;
193 |       if (!endMarkerNode.isExprResult()) {
194 |         compiler.report(
195 |             t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, endMarkerName));
196 |         return;
197 |       }
198 | 
199 |       if (markerStack.isEmpty()) {
200 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
201 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
202 |         return;
203 |       }
204 | 
205 |       Node startMarkerNode = markerStack.pop();
206 |       if (endMarkerNode.getParent() != startMarkerNode.getParent()) {
207 |         // The end marker isn't in the same block as the start marker.
208 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
209 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
210 |         return;
211 |       }
212 | 
213 |       // This is a valid marker set add it to the list of markers to process.
214 |       validMarkers.add(new Marker(startMarkerNode, endMarkerNode));
215 |     }

===== M0823 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 151-197
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
151 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
152 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
153 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.BLOCK:
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |       case Token.TRY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
184 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
185 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
186 |         } else {
187 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
188 |         }
189 |       case Token.SWITCH:
190 |       case Token.CASE:
191 |       case Token.CATCH:
192 |       case Token.WITH:
193 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |       default:
195 |         return false;
196 |     }
197 |   }
