===== M0829 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 785-929
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
785 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
786 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
787 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
788 |     // that we know to be safe
789 |     switch (n.getType()) {
790 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
791 |       case Token.AND:
792 |       case Token.BLOCK:
793 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
794 |       case Token.HOOK:
795 |       case Token.IF:
796 |       case Token.IN:
797 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
798 |       case Token.NUMBER:
799 |       case Token.OR:
800 |       case Token.THIS:
801 |       case Token.TRUE:
802 |       case Token.FALSE:
803 |       case Token.NULL:
804 |       case Token.STRING:
805 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
806 |       case Token.SWITCH:
807 |       case Token.TRY:
808 |       case Token.EMPTY:
809 |         break;
810 | 
811 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
812 |       case Token.THROW:
813 |         return true;
814 | 
815 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
816 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
817 |           return true;
818 |         }
819 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
820 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
821 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
822 |             return true;
823 |           }
824 |         }
825 |         return false;
826 | 
827 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
828 |       case Token.REGEXP:
829 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
830 |           return true;
831 |         }
832 |         break;
833 | 
834 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
835 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
836 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
837 |           return true;
838 |         }
839 |         break;
840 | 
841 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
842 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
843 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
844 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
845 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
846 | 
847 |       case Token.NEW:
848 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
849 |           return true;
850 |         }
851 | 
852 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
853 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
854 |           // side-effects
855 |           break;
856 |         }
857 |         return true;
858 | 
859 |       case Token.CALL:
860 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
861 |         // side effect property set.
862 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
863 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
864 |           // side-effects
865 |           break;
866 |         }
867 |         return true;
868 | 
869 |       default:
870 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
871 |           break;
872 |         }
873 | 
874 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
875 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
876 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
877 |             return true;
878 |           }
879 | 
880 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
881 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
882 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
883 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
884 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
885 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
886 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
887 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
888 |             return true;
889 |           }
890 | 
891 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
892 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
893 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
894 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
895 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
896 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
897 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
898 |               return false;
899 |             }
900 | 
901 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
902 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
903 |             // other objects.
904 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
905 |             // side-effect.
906 |             while (isGet(current)) {
907 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
908 |             }
909 | 
910 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
911 |           } else {
912 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
913 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
914 |             // preserve existing behavior.
915 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
916 |           }
917 |         }
918 | 
919 |         return true;
920 |     }
921 | 
922 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
923 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
924 |         return true;
925 |       }
926 |     }
927 | 
928 |     return false;
929 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.computeEscaped(Scope,Set<Var>,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 548-578
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in javascript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
555 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

318 |     @Override
319 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {

322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() < 2) {
325 |         return;
326 |       }
327 | 
328 |       int type = n.getType();
329 |       Var aliasVar = null;
330 |       if (type == Token.NAME) {
331 |         String name = n.getString();
332 |         Var lexicalVar = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
333 |         if (lexicalVar != null && lexicalVar == aliases.get(name)) {
334 |           aliasVar = lexicalVar;
335 |         }
336 |       }
337 | 
338 |       // Validate the top level of the goog.scope block.
339 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() == 2) {
340 |         if (aliasVar != null && NodeUtil.isLValue(n)) {
341 |           if (aliasVar.getNode() == n) {
342 |             aliasDefinitionsInOrder.add(n);
343 | 
344 |             // Return early, to ensure that we don't record a definition
345 |             // twice.
346 |             return;
347 |           } else {
348 |             report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_ALIAS_REDEFINED, n.getString());
349 |           }
350 |         }
351 | 
352 |         if (type == Token.RETURN) {
353 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_RETURN);
354 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
355 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_REFERENCES_THIS);
356 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
357 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
358 |         }
359 |       }
360 | 
361 |       // Validate all descendent scopes of the goog.scope block.
362 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {
363 |         // Check if this name points to an alias.
364 |         if (aliasVar != null) {
365 |           // Note, to support the transitive case, it's important we don't
366 |           // clone aliasedNode here.  For example,
367 |           // var g = goog; var d = g.dom; d.createElement('DIV');
368 |           // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the
369 |           // changes pass above with "goog".  If we cloned here, we'd end up
370 |           // with <code>g.dom.createElement('DIV')</code>.
371 |           Node aliasedNode = aliasVar.getInitialValue();
372 |           aliasUsages.add(new AliasedNode(n, aliasedNode));
373 |         }
374 | 
375 |         JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
376 |         if (info != null) {
377 |           for (Node node : info.getTypeNodes()) {
378 |             fixTypeNode(node);

   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';

377 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {

379 | 
380 |     if (callTarget == null || !callTarget.isGetProp()) {
381 |       return n;
382 |     }
383 |

392 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();

406 |     String joinString = (right == null) ? "," : NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
407 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
408 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
409 |     int foldedSize = 0;
410 |     Node prev = null;
411 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
412 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
413 |     while (elem != null) {
414 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem) || elem.isEmpty()) {
415 |         if (sb == null) {
416 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
417 |         } else {
418 |           sb.append(joinString);
419 |         }
420 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getArrayElementStringValue(elem));
421 |       } else {
422 |         if (sb != null) {
423 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
424 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
425 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
426 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
427 |               IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
428 |           sb = null;
429 |         }
430 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
431 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
432 |       }
433 |       prev = elem;
434 |       elem = elem.getNext();
435 |     }
436 | 
437 |     if (sb != null) {
438 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
439 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
440 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
441 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
442 |           IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
443 |     }
444 |     // one for each comma.
445 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
446 | 
447 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
448 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
449 |       case 0:
450 |         Node emptyStringNode = IR.string("");
451 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
452 |         reportCodeChange();

455 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
456 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
457 |           return n;

461 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
462 |           // it is coerced to a string.

469 |         reportCodeChange();

473 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
474 |           return n;

479 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {

806 |       }

197 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
198 |     List<Callback> passes = Lists.newArrayList();
199 |     if (removeAbstractMethods) {
200 |       passes.add(new FindAbstractMethods());
201 |     }
202 |     if (removeAssertionCalls) {
203 |       passes.add(new FindAssertionCalls());
204 |     }
205 |     CombinedCompilerPass.traverse(compiler, root, passes);
206 | 
207 |     for (RemovableAssignment assignment : abstractMethodAssignmentNodes) {
208 |       assignment.remove();
209 |     }

212 |       // If the assertion is an expression, just strip the whole thing.
213 |       Node parent = call.getParent();
214 |       if (parent.isExprResult()) {
215 |         parent.getParent().removeChild(parent);
216 |       } else {
217 |         // Otherwise, replace the assertion with its first argument,
218 |         // which is the return value of the assertion.
219 |         Node firstArg = call.getFirstChild().getNext();
220 |         if (firstArg == null) {
221 |           parent.replaceChild(call, NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(call));
222 |         } else {

224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();

/**
   * Determines if n matches the type and name for the following types of
   * "exits":
   *    - return without values
   *    - continues and breaks with or without names.
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param type The Token type to look for.
   * @param labelName The name that must be associated with the exit type.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks associated with labels.
   * @return Whether the node matches the specified block-exit type.
   */
Method code:
284 |   static private boolean matchingExitNode(Node n, int type, String labelName) {
285 |     if (n.getType() == type) {
286 |       if (type == Token.RETURN) {
287 |         // only returns without expressions.
288 |         return !n.hasChildren();
289 |       } else {
290 |         if (labelName == null) {
291 |           return !n.hasChildren();
292 |         } else {
293 |           return n.hasChildren()
294 |             && labelName.equals(n.getFirstChild().getString());
295 |         }
296 |       }
297 |     }
298 |     return false;
299 |   }

Method code:
240 |   void addNumber(double x) {
241 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
242 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
243 |     char prev = getLastChar();
244 |     boolean negativeZero = isNegativeZero(x);
245 |     if ((x < 0 || negativeZero) && prev == '-') {
246 |       add(" ");
247 |     }
248 | 
249 |     if ((long) x == x && !negativeZero) {
250 |       long value = (long) x;
251 |       long mantissa = value;
252 |       int exp = 0;
253 |       if (Math.abs(x) >= 100) {
254 |         while (mantissa / 10 * Math.pow(10, exp + 1) == value) {
255 |           mantissa /= 10;
256 |           exp++;
257 |         }
258 |       }
259 |       if (exp > 2) {
260 |         add(Long.toString(mantissa) + "E" + Integer.toString(exp));
261 |       } else {
262 |         add(Long.toString(value));
263 |       }
264 |     } else {
265 |       add(String.valueOf(x));
266 |     }
267 |   }

   * Calculates the minimum number of occurrences of throw needed to alias
   * throw.

Method code:
199 |   static int estimateMinOccurrencesRequriedToAlias() {
200 |     // Assuming that the alias function name is two bytes in length, two bytes
201 |     // will be saved per occurrence of throw:

206 |     // Hence there must be more than N/2 occurrences of throw to reduce
207 |     // the code size.
208 |     Node alias = createAliasFunctionNode("TT");
209 |     return InlineCostEstimator.getCost(alias) / 2 + 1;
210 |   }

===== M1013 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 184-275
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
184 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
185 |       boolean conditional) {
186 | 
187 |     switch (n.getType()) {
188 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
189 |       case Token.BLOCK:
190 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
191 |         return;
192 | 
193 |       case Token.WHILE:
194 |       case Token.DO:
195 |       case Token.IF:
196 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
197 |             conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.FOR:
201 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
202 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
203 |               conditional);
204 |         } else {
205 |           // for(x in y) {...}
206 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
207 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
208 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
209 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
210 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
211 |           }
212 | 
213 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
214 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
215 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
216 |           } else {
217 |             computeGenKill(lhs, gen, kill, conditional);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // rhs is executed only once so we don't go into it every loop.
221 |         }
222 |         return;
223 | 
224 |       case Token.VAR:
225 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
226 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
227 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
228 |             if (!conditional) {
229 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
230 |             }
231 |           }
232 |         }
233 |         return;
234 | 
235 |       case Token.AND:
236 |       case Token.OR:
237 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
238 |         // May short circuit.
239 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
240 |         return;
241 | 
242 |       case Token.HOOK:
243 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
244 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
245 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
246 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
247 |         return;
248 | 
249 |       case Token.NAME:
250 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
251 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
252 |         } else {
253 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       default:
258 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
259 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
260 |           if (!conditional) {
261 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
262 |           }
263 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
264 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
265 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
266 |           }
267 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
268 |         } else {
269 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
270 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
271 |           }
272 |         }
273 |         return;
274 |     }
275 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.getLocalVarIndex(Var)

/**
   * Returns the index within the scope stack.
   * e.g. function Foo(a) { var b; function c(d) { } }
   * a = 0, b = 1, c = 2, d = 3
   */
Method code:
545 |   private int getLocalVarIndex(Var v) {
546 |     int num = v.index;
547 |     Scope s = v.scope.getParent();
548 |     if (s == null) {
549 |       throw new IllegalArgumentException("Var is not local");
550 |     }
551 | 
552 |     boolean isBleedingIntoScope = s.getParent() != null &&
553 |         localBleedingFunctions.contains(v);
554 |

556 |       if (isBleedingIntoScope) {
557 |         num += localBleedingFunctionsPerScope.get(s).indexOf(v) + 1;
558 |         isBleedingIntoScope = false;

561 |       }
562 |

564 |       s = s.getParent();
565 |     }
566 |     return num;

/**
     * Returns the name of a prototype property being assigned to this r-value.
     *

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.recordAlias(String,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1055-1087
Documentation:
/**
   * Records an alias of one name to another name.
   */
Method code:
1055 |   private void recordAlias(String fromName, String toName) {
1056 |     recordReference(fromName, toName, RefType.REGULAR);
1057 | 
1058 |     // We need to add an edge to the alias graph. The alias graph is expressed
1059 |     // implicitly as a set of connected components, called AliasSets.
1060 |     //
1061 |     // There are three possibilities:
1062 |     // 1) Neither name is part of a connected component. Create a new one.
1063 |     // 2) Exactly one name is part of a connected component. Merge the new
1064 |     //    name into the component.
1065 |     // 3) The two names are already part of connected components. Merge
1066 |     //    those components together.
1067 |     AliasSet toNameAliasSet = aliases.get(toName);
1068 |     AliasSet fromNameAliasSet = aliases.get(fromName);
1069 |     AliasSet resultSet = null;
1070 |     if (toNameAliasSet == null && fromNameAliasSet == null) {
1071 |       resultSet = new AliasSet(toName, fromName);
1072 |     } else if (toNameAliasSet != null && fromNameAliasSet != null) {
1073 |       resultSet = toNameAliasSet;
1074 |       resultSet.names.addAll(fromNameAliasSet.names);
1075 |       for (String name : fromNameAliasSet.names) {
1076 |         aliases.put(name, resultSet);
1077 |       }
1078 |     } else if (toNameAliasSet != null) {
1079 |       resultSet = toNameAliasSet;
1080 |       resultSet.names.add(fromName);
1081 |     } else {
1082 |       resultSet = fromNameAliasSet;
1083 |       resultSet.names.add(toName);
1084 |     }
1085 |     aliases.put(fromName, resultSet);
1086 |     aliases.put(toName, resultSet);
1087 |   }

484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;
492 |     }
493 | 
494 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
496 | 
497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
498 |     // function (unless it is called)
499 |     while (child != null && child.isFunction()) {
500 |       child = child.getNext();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     if (child != null) {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
505 |     } else {
506 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
507 |     }
508 | 
509 |     // Synthetic blocks
510 |     if (parent != null) {
511 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
512 |         case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:
515 |           break;
516 |         default:
517 |           if (node.isBlock() && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
518 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
519 |           }
520 |           break;
521 |       }
522 |     }
523 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.TransformDispatcher.processStringLiteral(StringLiteral)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 910-937

Method code:
910 |     @Override
911 |     Node processStringLiteral(StringLiteral literalNode) {
912 |       String value = literalNode.getValue();
913 |       Node n = newStringNode(value);
914 |       if (value.indexOf('\u000B') != -1) {
915 |         // NOTE(nicksantos): In JavaScript, there are 3 ways to
916 |         // represent a vertical tab: \v, \x0B, \u000B.
917 |         // The \v notation was added later, and is not understood
918 |         // on IE. So we need to preserve it as-is. This is really
919 |         // obnoxious, because we do not have a good way to represent
920 |         // how the original string was encoded without making the
921 |         // representation of strings much more complicated.
922 |         //
923 |         // To handle this, we look at the original source test, and
924 |         // mark the string as \v-encoded or not. If a string is
925 |         // \v encoded, then all the vertical tabs in that string
926 |         // will be encoded with a \v.
927 |         int start = literalNode.getAbsolutePosition();
928 |         int end = start + literalNode.getLength();
929 |         if (start < sourceString.length() &&
930 |             (sourceString.substring(
931 |                  start, Math.min(sourceString.length(), end))
932 |              .indexOf("\\v") != -1)) {
933 |           n.putBooleanProp(Node.SLASH_V, true);
934 |         }
935 |       }
936 |       return n;
937 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameProperties.anonymous_L101.compare(Property,Property)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameProperties.java
Original range: 102-125
Documentation:

Method code:
102 |       @Override
103 |       public int compare(Property p1, Property p2) {
104 | 
105 |         /**
106 |          * First a frequently used names would always be picked first.
107 |          */
108 |         if (p1.numOccurrences != p2.numOccurrences) {
109 |           return p2.numOccurrences - p1.numOccurrences;
110 | 
111 |         /**
112 |          * If both properties are used equally frequent. We'll let the property
113 |          * with a high affinity score get a name first.
114 |          *
115 |          * see #computeAffinityScores() for how the score is computed.
116 |          */
117 |         } else if (p1.affinityScore != p2.affinityScore) {
118 |           return p2.affinityScore - p1.affinityScore;
119 |         }
120 | 
121 |         /**
122 |          * Finally, for determinism, we compare them based on the old name.
123 |          */
124 |         return p1.oldName.compareTo(p2.oldName);
125 |        }

1105 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {
1106 |     // First check if escaping is needed at all -- in most cases it isn't.
1107 |     if (NodeUtil.isLatin(s)) {
1108 |       return s;
1109 |     }
1110 |

1112 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
1113 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1114 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1115 |       // Identifiers should always go to Latin1/ ASCII characters because
1116 |       // different browser's rules for valid identifier characters are
1117 |       // crazy.
1118 |       if (c > 0x1F && c < 0x7F) {

1120 |       } else {
1121 |         appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1122 |       }
1123 |     }
1124 |     return sb.toString();
1125 |   }

===== M1122 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 989-991
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
989 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
990 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
991 |   }

===== M1134 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.
499 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
500 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
501 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
502 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
503 |       }
504 | 
505 |       // Now, make the assignments
506 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
507 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
508 |         ++i;
509 |       }
510 |     }
511 |   }

===== M1142 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(NodeTraversal,ControlFlowGraph<Node>,Set<Var>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 212-305
Documentation:

Method code:
212 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
213 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
214 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
215 |         LinkedUndirectedGraph.create();
216 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
217 | 
218 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
219 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
220 |       Var v = i.next();
221 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
222 | 
223 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
224 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
225 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
226 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
227 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
228 |         // around with it.
229 |         if (!v.getParentNode().isFunction()) {
230 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
231 |         }
232 |       }
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
236 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
237 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
238 | 
239 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
240 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
241 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
242 | 
243 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
244 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
245 |           continue;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
249 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
250 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
251 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
252 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
253 |         }
254 | 
255 |         if (v1.getParentNode().isParamList() &&
256 |             v2.getParentNode().isParamList()) {
257 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
258 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
259 |         }
260 | 
261 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
262 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
263 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
264 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
265 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
266 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
267 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
268 |           }
269 | 
270 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
271 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
272 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
273 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
274 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
275 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
276 |           }
277 |         }
278 | 
279 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
280 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
281 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
282 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
283 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
284 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
285 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
286 |           }
287 | 
288 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
289 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
290 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
291 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
292 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
293 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
294 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
295 |               compiler,
296 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
297 |               checker);
298 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
299 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
300 |           }
301 |         }
302 |       }
303 |     }
304 |     return interferenceGraph;
305 |   }

   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread

429 |       return 0;

===== M1152 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 75-166
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
75 |   @Override
76 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
77 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
78 |     switch(node.getType()) {
79 |       case Token.RETURN: {
80 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
81 |         if (result != node) {
82 |           return result;
83 |         }
84 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
85 |         if (result != node) {
86 |           return result;
87 |         }
88 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
89 |       }
90 | 
91 |       case Token.THROW: {
92 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
93 |         if (result != node) {
94 |           return result;
95 |         }
96 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
97 |       }
98 | 
99 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
100 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
101 | 
102 |       case Token.NOT:
103 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
104 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
105 | 
106 |       case Token.IF:
107 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
108 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
111 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
112 |         return node;
113 | 
114 |       case Token.HOOK:
115 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
116 |         return node;
117 | 
118 |       case Token.WHILE:
119 |       case Token.DO:
120 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
121 |         return node;
122 | 
123 |       case Token.FOR:
124 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
125 |           tryJoinForCondition(node);
126 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
127 |         }
128 |         return node;
129 | 
130 |       case Token.TRUE:
131 |       case Token.FALSE:
132 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
133 | 
134 |       case Token.NEW:
135 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
136 |         if (!node.isCall()) {
137 |           return node;
138 |         }
139 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
140 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
141 |       case Token.CALL:
142 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
143 |         if (result == node) {
144 |           result = tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(node);
145 |           if (result == node) {
146 |             result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         return result;
150 | 
151 |       case Token.COMMA:
152 |         return trySplitComma(node);
153 | 
154 |       case Token.NAME:
155 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
156 | 
157 |       case Token.BLOCK:
158 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
162 | 
163 |       default:
164 |         return node; //Nothing changed
165 |     }
166 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)

Original range: 125-146
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
125 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
126 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
127 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
128 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
129 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
130 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
131 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
132 | 
133 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
134 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
135 |         }
136 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
137 |       } else {
138 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
139 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 | 
143 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
144 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
145 |     }
146 |   }

===== M1180 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseFunction(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeTraversal.java
Original range: 510-545
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses a function.
   */
Method code:
510 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
511 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
512 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isFunction());
513 | 
514 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
515 | 
516 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
517 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
518 | 
519 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
520 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
521 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
522 |     }
523 | 
524 |     curNode = n;
525 |     pushScope(n);
526 | 
527 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
528 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
529 |       // scope.
530 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
531 |     }
532 | 
533 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
534 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
535 | 
536 |     // Args
537 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
538 | 
539 |     // Body
540 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
541 |             body.isBlock(), body);
542 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
543 | 
544 |     popScope();
545 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessClosurePrimitives.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessClosurePrimitives.java
Original range: 175-266
Documentation:

Method code:
175 |   @Override
176 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
177 |     switch (n.getType()) {
178 |       case Token.CALL:
179 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
180 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
181 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
182 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
183 |           if (name.isName() &&
184 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
185 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
186 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
187 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
188 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
189 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
190 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
191 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
192 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
193 |               break;
194 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
195 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
196 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
197 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
198 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
199 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
200 |               if (arg.isString()) {
201 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
202 |                 if (dot == -1) {
203 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
204 |                 } else {
205 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
206 |                 }
207 |               }
208 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
209 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
210 |               List<String> typeDecls =
211 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
212 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
213 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
214 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
215 |                 }
216 |               }
217 | 
218 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
219 |               // get compiled out.
220 |               parent.replaceChild(n, IR.number(0));
221 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
222 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
223 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
224 |             }
225 |           }
226 |         }
227 |         break;
228 | 
229 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
230 |       case Token.NAME:
231 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
232 |         // object.
233 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
234 |         break;
235 | 
236 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
237 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);
238 |         break;
239 | 
240 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
241 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
242 |         // error. Hosited functions will explode if the're provided.
243 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
244 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
245 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
246 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
247 |           if (pn != null) {
248 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
249 |           }
250 |         }
251 |         break;
252 | 
253 |       case Token.NEW:
254 |         trySimplifyNewDate(t, n, parent);
255 |         break;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.GETPROP:
258 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isName() &&
259 |             !parent.isCall() &&
260 |             !parent.isAssign() &&
261 |             "goog.base".equals(n.getQualifiedName())) {
262 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
263 |         }
264 |         break;
265 |     }
266 |   }

===== M1206 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameProperties.ProcessProperties.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameProperties.java
Original range: 406-471
Documentation:

Method code:
406 |     @Override
407 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
408 |       switch (n.getType()) {
409 |         case Token.GETPROP:
410 |           Node propNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
411 |           if (propNode.isString()) {
412 |             maybeMarkCandidate(propNode);
413 |           }
414 |           break;
415 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
416 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
417 |             if (!key.isQuotedString()) {
418 |               maybeMarkCandidate(key);
419 |             } else {
420 |               // Ensure that we never rename some other property in a way
421 |               // that could conflict with this quoted key.
422 |               quotedNames.add(key.getString());
423 |             }
424 |           }
425 |           break;
426 |         case Token.GETELEM:
427 |           // If this is a quoted property access (e.g. x['myprop']), we need to
428 |           // ensure that we never rename some other property in a way that
429 |           // could conflict with this quoted name.
430 |           Node child = n.getLastChild();
431 |           if (child != null && child.isString()) {
432 |             quotedNames.add(child.getString());
433 |           }
434 |           break;
435 |         case Token.CALL:
436 |           // We replace a JSCompiler_renameProperty function call with a string
437 |           // containing the renamed property.
438 |           Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
439 |           if (fnName.isName() &&
440 |               RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(fnName.getString())) {
441 |             callNodeToParentMap.put(n, parent);
442 |             countCallCandidates(t, n);
443 |           }
444 |           break;
445 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
446 |           // We eliminate any stub implementations of JSCompiler_renameProperty
447 |           // that we encounter.
448 |           if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
449 |             String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
450 |             if (RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(name)) {
451 |               if (parent.isExprResult()) {
452 |                 parent.detachFromParent();
453 |               } else {
454 |                 parent.removeChild(n);
455 |               }
456 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
457 |             }
458 |           } else if (parent.isName() &&
459 |                      RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(parent.getString())) {
460 |             Node varNode = parent.getParent();
461 |             if (varNode.isVar()) {
462 |               varNode.removeChild(parent);
463 |               if (!varNode.hasChildren()) {
464 |                 varNode.detachFromParent();
465 |               }
466 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
467 |             }
468 |           }
469 |           break;
470 |       }
471 |     }

     * There are two types of calls we are interested in calls without explicit
     * "this" values (what we are call "free" calls) and direct call to eval.

===== M1227 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2895-2959
Documentation:
/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2895 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2896 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2897 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2898 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2899 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2900 |         // value is immutable.
2901 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2902 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2903 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2904 |       case Token.COMMA:
2905 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2906 |       case Token.AND:
2907 |       case Token.OR:
2908 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2909 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2910 |       case Token.HOOK:
2911 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2912 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2913 |       case Token.INC:
2914 |       case Token.DEC:
2915 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2916 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2917 |         } else {
2918 |           return true;
2919 |         }
2920 |       case Token.THIS:
2921 |         return locals.apply(value);
2922 |       case Token.NAME:
2923 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2924 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2925 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2926 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2927 |         return locals.apply(value);
2928 |       case Token.CALL:
2929 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2930 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2931 |             || locals.apply(value);
2932 |       case Token.NEW:
2933 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2934 |                || locals.apply(value);
2935 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2936 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2937 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2938 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2939 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2940 |         return true;
2941 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2942 |       case Token.IN:
2943 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2944 |         return true;
2945 |       default:
2946 |         // Other op force a local value:
2947 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2948 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2949 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2950 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2951 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2952 |           return true;
2953 |         }
2954 | 
2955 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2956 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2957 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2958 |     }
2959 |   }

===== M1267 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineObjectLiterals.InliningBehavior.isInlinableObject(List<Reference>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineObjectLiterals.java
Original range: 155-240
Documentation:
/**
     * Counts the number of direct (full) references to an object.
     * Specifically we check for references of the following type:
     * <pre>
     *   x;
     *   x.fn();
     * </pre>
     */
Method code:
155 |     private boolean isInlinableObject(List<Reference> refs) {
156 |       boolean ret = false;
157 |       for (Reference ref : refs) {
158 |         Node name = ref.getNode();
159 |         Node parent = ref.getParent();
160 |         Node gramps = ref.getGrandparent();
161 | 
162 |         // Ignore indirect references, like x.y (except x.y(), since
163 |         // the function referenced by y might reference 'this').
164 |         //
165 |         if (parent.isGetProp()) {
166 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.getFirstChild() == name);
167 |           // A call target maybe using the object as a 'this' value.
168 |           if (gramps.isCall()
169 |               && gramps.getFirstChild() == parent) {
170 |             return false;
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): This pass's object-splitting algorithm has
174 |           // a blind spot. It assumes that if a property isn't defined on an
175 |           // object, then the value is undefined. This is not true, because
176 |           // Object.prototype can have arbitrary properties on it.
177 |           //
178 |           // We short-circuit this problem by bailing out if we see a reference
179 |           // to a property that isn't defined on the object literal. This
180 |           // isn't a perfect algorithm, but it should catch most cases.
181 |           continue;
182 |         }
183 | 
184 |         // Only rewrite VAR declarations or simple assignment statements
185 |         if (!isVarOrAssignExprLhs(name)) {
186 |            return false;
187 |         }
188 | 
189 |         Node val = ref.getAssignedValue();
190 |         if (val == null) {
191 |           // A var with no assignment.
192 |           continue;
193 |         }
194 | 
195 |         // We're looking for object literal assignments only.
196 |         if (!val.isObjectLit()) {
197 |           return false;
198 |         }
199 | 
200 |         // Make sure that the value is not self-refential. IOW,
201 |         // disallow things like x = {b: x.a}.
202 |         //
203 |         // TODO: Only exclude unorderable self-referential
204 |         // assignments. i.e. x = {a: x.b, b: x.a} is not orderable,
205 |         // but x = {a: 1, b: x.a} is.
206 |         //
207 |         // Also, ES5 getters/setters aren't handled by this pass.
208 |         for (Node child = val.getFirstChild(); child != null;
209 |              child = child.getNext()) {
210 |           if (child.isGetterDef() ||
211 |               child.isSetterDef()) {
212 |             // ES5 get/set not supported.
213 |             return false;
214 |           }
215 | 
216 | 
217 |           Node childVal = child.getFirstChild();
218 |           // Check if childVal is the parent of any of the passed in
219 |           // references, as that is how self-referential assignments
220 |           // will happen.
221 |           for (Reference t : refs) {
222 |             Node refNode = t.getParent();
223 |             while (!NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(refNode)) {
224 |               if (refNode == childVal) {
225 |                 // There's a self-referential assignment
226 |                 return false;
227 |               }
228 |               refNode = refNode.getParent();
229 |             }
230 |           }
231 |         }
232 | 
233 | 
234 |         // We have found an acceptable object literal assignment. As
235 |         // long as there are no other assignments that mess things up,
236 |         // we can inline.
237 |         ret = true;
238 |       }
239 |       return ret;
240 |     }

   * Merge a block with its parent block.

1821 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.isBlock());
1822 |     Node parent = block.getParent();
1823 |     // Try to remove the block if its parent is a block/script or if its
1824 |     // parent is label and it has exactly one child.

/**
   * Runs through all namespaces (prefixes of classes and enums), and checks if
   * any of them have been used in an unsafe way.
   */
Method code:
249 |   private void checkNamespaces() {
250 |     for (Name name : nameMap.values()) {
251 |       if (name.isNamespace() &&
252 |           (name.aliasingGets > 0 || name.localSets + name.globalSets > 1 ||
253 |            name.deleteProps > 0)) {
254 |         boolean initialized = name.getDeclaration() != null;

256 |           if (ref == name.getDeclaration()) {
257 |             continue;

259 |

261 |             if (initialized) {
262 |               warnAboutNamespaceRedefinition(name, ref);
263 |             }
264 |           } else if (
265 |               ref.type == Ref.Type.SET_FROM_GLOBAL ||
266 |               ref.type == Ref.Type.SET_FROM_LOCAL) {
267 |             if (initialized) {
268 |               warnAboutNamespaceRedefinition(name, ref);
269 |             }
270 | 
271 |             initialized = true;
272 |           } else if (ref.type == Ref.Type.ALIASING_GET) {
273 |             warnAboutNamespaceAliasing(name, ref);
274 |           }
275 |         }

   * Tells the type system that {@code owner} may have a property named
   * {@code propertyName}. This allows the registry to keep track of what
   * types a property is defined upon.
   *
   * This is NOT the same as saying that {@code owner} must have a property
   * named type. ObjectType#hasProperty attempts to minimize false positives
   * ("if we're not sure, then don't type check this property"). The type
   * registry, on the other hand, should attempt to minimize false negatives

===== M1315 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.strEscape(String,char,String,String,String,CharsetEncoder,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1016-1103
Documentation:
/** Helper to escape javascript string as well as regular expression */
Method code:
1016 |   private static String strEscape(
1017 |       String s, char quote,
1018 |       String doublequoteEscape,
1019 |       String singlequoteEscape,
1020 |       String backslashEscape,
1021 |       CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder,
1022 |       boolean useSlashV) {
1023 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 2);
1024 |     sb.append(quote);
1025 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1026 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1027 |       switch (c) {
1028 |         case '\0': sb.append("\\x00"); break;
1029 |         case '\u000B':
1030 |           if (useSlashV) {
1031 |             sb.append("\\v");
1032 |           } else {
1033 |             sb.append("\\x0B");
1034 |           }
1035 |           break;
1036 |         // From the SingleEscapeCharacter grammar production.
1037 |         case '\b': sb.append("\\b"); break;
1038 |         case '\f': sb.append("\\f"); break;
1039 |         case '\n': sb.append("\\n"); break;
1040 |         case '\r': sb.append("\\r"); break;
1041 |         case '\t': sb.append("\\t"); break;
1042 |         case '\\': sb.append(backslashEscape); break;
1043 |         case '\"': sb.append(doublequoteEscape); break;
1044 |         case '\'': sb.append(singlequoteEscape); break;
1045 | 
1046 |         // From LineTerminators (ES5 Section 7.3, Table 3)
1047 |         case '\u2028': sb.append("\\u2028"); break;
1048 |         case '\u2029': sb.append("\\u2029"); break;
1049 | 
1050 |         case '>':                       // Break --> into --\> or ]]> into ]]\>
1051 |           if (i >= 2 &&
1052 |               ((s.charAt(i - 1) == '-' && s.charAt(i - 2) == '-') ||
1053 |                (s.charAt(i - 1) == ']' && s.charAt(i - 2) == ']'))) {
1054 |             sb.append("\\>");
1055 |           } else {
1056 |             sb.append(c);
1057 |           }
1058 |           break;
1059 |         case '<':
1060 |           // Break </script into <\/script
1061 |           final String END_SCRIPT = "/script";
1062 | 
1063 |           // Break <!-- into <\!--
1064 |           final String START_COMMENT = "!--";
1065 | 
1066 |           if (s.regionMatches(true, i + 1, END_SCRIPT, 0,
1067 |                               END_SCRIPT.length())) {
1068 |             sb.append("<\\");
1069 |           } else if (s.regionMatches(false, i + 1, START_COMMENT, 0,
1070 |                                      START_COMMENT.length())) {
1071 |             sb.append("<\\");
1072 |           } else {
1073 |             sb.append(c);
1074 |           }
1075 |           break;
1076 |         default:
1077 |           // If we're given an outputCharsetEncoder, then check if the
1078 |           //  character can be represented in this character set.
1079 |           if (outputCharsetEncoder != null) {
1080 |             if (outputCharsetEncoder.canEncode(c)) {
1081 |               sb.append(c);
1082 |             } else {
1083 |               // Unicode-escape the character.
1084 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1085 |             }
1086 |           } else {
1087 |             // No charsetEncoder provided - pass straight latin characters
1088 |             // through, and escape the rest.  Doing the explicit character
1089 |             // check is measurably faster than using the CharsetEncoder.
1090 |             if (c > 0x1f && c < 0x7f) {
1091 |               sb.append(c);
1092 |             } else {
1093 |               // Other characters can be misinterpreted by some js parsers,
1094 |               // or perhaps mangled by proxies along the way,
1095 |               // so we play it safe and unicode escape them.
1096 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1097 |             }
1098 |           }
1099 |       }
1100 |     }
1101 |     sb.append(quote);
1102 |     return sb.toString();
1103 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.GatherCollapses.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 136-179
Documentation:

Method code:
136 |     @Override
137 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
138 |       if (n.isVar()) {
139 |         blacklistStubVars(t, n);
140 |       }
141 | 
142 |       // Only care about var nodes
143 |       if (!n.isVar() && !canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope())) return;
144 | 
145 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
146 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
147 | 
148 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
149 |       // be collapsed
150 |       if (parent.isIf()) return;
151 | 
152 |       Node varNode = n;
153 | 
154 |       boolean hasVar = n.isVar();
155 | 
156 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
157 |       n = n.getNext();
158 | 
159 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
160 | 
161 |       while (n != null &&
162 |           (n.isVar() || canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope()))) {
163 | 
164 |         if (n.isVar()) {
165 |           blacklistStubVars(t, n);
166 |           hasVar = true;
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
170 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
171 | 
172 |         n = n.getNext();
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse && hasVar) {
176 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
177 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, n, parent));
178 |       }
179 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 147-210
Documentation:

Method code:
147 |   @Override
148 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
149 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !n.isName() ||
150 |         parent.isFunction()) {
151 |       // Don't rename named functions.
152 |       return;
153 |     }
154 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
155 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
156 |     if (vNode == null) {
157 |       // This is not a local.
158 |       return;
159 |     }
160 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
161 | 
162 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
163 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
164 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
165 |         return;
166 |       }
167 | 
168 |       // Rename.
169 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
170 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
171 | 
172 |       if (parent.isVar()) {
173 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
174 |       }
175 |     } else {
176 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
177 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
178 |       // make this fast.
179 |       String pseudoName = null;
180 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
181 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
182 |         Var iVar = i.next();
183 | 
184 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
185 |         // and it is merged with the current coalscedVar.
186 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
187 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
188 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
189 |         }
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       // Keep its original name.
193 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
194 |         return;
195 |       }
196 | 
197 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
198 | 
199 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
200 |         pseudoName += "$";
201 |       }
202 | 
203 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
204 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
205 | 
206 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && parent.isVar()) {
207 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
208 |       }
209 |     }
210 |   }

===== M1344 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 35-82
Documentation:

Method code:
35 |   @Override
36 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
37 |     if (!subtree.isScript() && !subtree.isBlock()) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (!child.isVar() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (!name.isName()) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 83-166

Method code:
83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
86 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.
89 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||
90 |         n.isComma()) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (parent == null) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     int pt = parent.getType();
99 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
100 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
101 |       if (gramps.isCall() &&
102 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
103 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
104 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
105 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
106 |         // an eval.
107 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
108 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
109 |             n.getNext().isName() &&
110 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
111 |           return;
112 |         }
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
116 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
117 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
118 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
119 |             continue;
120 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
121 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
122 |             return;
123 |           else
124 |             break;
125 |         }
126 |       }
127 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
128 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
129 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
130 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
131 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
132 |         // of a for.
133 |       } else {
134 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
135 |       }
136 |     }
137 | 
138 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType());
139 |     if (isSimpleOp ||
140 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
141 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
142 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
143 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
144 |         return;
145 |       } else if (n.isExprResult()) {
146 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
147 |         return;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
151 |       if (n.isString()) {
152 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
153 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
154 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Token.name(n.getType()).toLowerCase() +
155 |             "' operator is not being used.";
156 |       }
157 | 
158 |       t.getCompiler().report(
159 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
160 |       // TODO(johnlenz): determine if it is necessary to
161 |       // try to protect side-effect free statements as well.
162 |       if (!NodeUtil.isStatement(n)) {
163 |         problemNodes.add(n);
164 |       }
165 |     }
166 |   }

===== M1415 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.maybeEscapedOrModifiedArguments(Scope,ReferenceMap)

Method code:
224 |     private boolean maybeEscapedOrModifiedArguments(
225 |         Scope scope, ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
226 |       if (scope.isLocal()) {
227 |         Var arguments = scope.getArgumentsVar();
228 |         ReferenceCollection refs = referenceMap.getReferences(arguments);
229 |         if (refs != null && !refs.references.isEmpty()) {
230 |           for (Reference ref : refs.references) {
231 |             Node refNode = ref.getNode();
232 |             Node refParent = ref.getParent();
233 |             // Any reference that is not a read of the arguments property
234 |             // consider a escape of the arguments object.
235 |             if (!(NodeUtil.isGet(refParent)
236 |                 && refNode == ref.getParent().getFirstChild()
237 |                 && !isLValue(refParent))) {
238 |               return true;
239 |             }
240 |           }
241 |         }
242 |       }
243 |       return false;
244 |     }
