===== M1455 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

===== M1461 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1683-1724
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1683 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1684 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1685 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1686 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1687 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1688 |       // {?} - right curly
1689 |       // {?=} - equals
1690 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1691 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1692 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1693 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1694 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1695 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1696 |       token = next();
1697 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1698 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1699 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1700 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1701 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1702 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1703 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1704 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1705 |       }
1706 | 
1707 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1708 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1709 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1710 |     } else {
1711 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1712 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1713 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1714 |           next();
1715 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1716 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1717 |           next();
1718 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1719 |         }
1720 |       }
1721 | 
1722 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1723 |     }
1724 |   }

108 |     if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isSimpleFunctionDeclaration(rValue)) {
109 |       return false;
110 |     }
111 | 
112 |     // Assume an exported method result is used.
113 |     if (!defFinder.canModifyDefinition(definition)) {
114 |       return false;
115 |     }
116 | 
117 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
118 | 
119 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
120 |       return false;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
124 |       // Any non-call reference maybe introducing an alias. Don't try to
125 |       // change the function signature, if all the aliases can't also be
126 |       // changed.
127 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Support .call signature changes.
128 |       if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isCallOrNewSite(site)) {
129 |         return false;
130 |       }
131 | 
132 |       // TODO(johnlenz): support specialization
133 | 
134 |       // Multiple definitions prevent rewrite.
135 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Allow rewrite all definitions are valid.
136 |       Node nameNode = site.node;
137 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
138 |           defFinder.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
139 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
140 |         return false;
141 |       }
142 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
143 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
144 |     }
145 | 
146 |     return true;
147 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:

2403 |     int len = s.length();
2404 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2405 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2406 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2407 |         return false;
2408 |       }
2409 |     }
2410 |     return true;
2411 |   }

===== M1483 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 192-296
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
192 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
193 |     int type = n.getType();
194 |     Var var = null;
195 |     switch (type) {
196 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
197 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
198 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
199 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
200 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
201 |         }
202 | 
203 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
204 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
205 |         } else {
206 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
207 |         }
208 |         return;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
211 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
212 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
213 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
214 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
215 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
216 |           if (var != null) {
217 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
218 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
219 | 
220 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
221 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
222 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
223 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
224 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
225 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
226 |               return;
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         break;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.CALL:
233 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
234 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
235 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
236 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
237 |           Var subclassVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
238 |           // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
239 |           // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
240 |           // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
241 |           // easier and mostly the same.
242 |           if (subclassVar != null && subclassVar.isGlobal()
243 |               && !referenced.contains(subclassVar)) {
244 |             // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
245 |             inheritsCalls.put(subclassVar, parent);
246 |             continuations.put(subclassVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
247 |             return;
248 |           }
249 |         }
250 |         break;
251 | 
252 |       case Token.NAME:
253 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
254 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
255 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
256 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
257 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
258 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
259 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
260 |             // of traversing immediately.
261 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
262 |             return;
263 |           }
264 |         } else {
265 | 
266 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
267 |           // on all the parameters.
268 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
269 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
270 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
271 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
272 |             }
273 |           }
274 | 
275 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
276 |           // are references to other vars.
277 |           if (var != null) {
278 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
279 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
280 |             // for now.
281 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
282 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
283 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
284 |               }
285 |             } else {
286 |               markReferencedVar(var);
287 |             }
288 |           }
289 |         }
290 |         break;
291 |     }
292 | 
293 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
294 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
295 |     }
296 |   }

Method code:
113 |   private void traverse(Node node) {
114 |     // The goal here is to avoid retraversing
115 |     // the entire AST to catch newly created opportunities.
116 |     // So we track whether a "unit of code" has changed,
117 |     // and revisit immediately.
118 |     if (!shouldVisit(node)) {
119 |       return;
120 |     }
121 |

125 |         traverse(c);
126 |       }
127 | 
128 |       visit(node);
129 |       visits++;
130 |

132 |     } while (shouldRetraverse(node));
133 |

===== M1492 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 114-205
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
114 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
115 | 
116 |     // Just an 'exit'.
117 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
118 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
119 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
120 |       return;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Just an 'if'.
124 |     if (n.isIf()) {
125 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
126 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
127 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
128 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
129 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
130 |       }
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 | 
134 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
135 |     if (n.isTry()) {
136 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
137 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
138 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
139 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
140 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
141 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
142 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
143 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
144 |       }
145 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
146 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
147 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     // Just a 'label'.
152 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
153 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
154 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
155 |     }
156 | 
157 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
158 | 
159 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
160 |     if (!n.isBlock() || n.getLastChild() == null) {
161 |       return;
162 |     }
163 | 
164 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
165 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
166 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
167 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
168 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
169 | 
170 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
171 |       if (c.isIf()) {
172 |         Node ifTree = c;
173 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
174 | 
175 |         // First, the true condition block.
176 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
177 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
178 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
179 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
180 | 
181 |         // Now the else block.
182 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
183 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
184 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
185 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
186 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
187 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 | 
191 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
192 |         break;
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
197 |     // look at what has become the last child.
198 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
199 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
200 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
201 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
202 |         break;
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeReturns.callResultsMaybeUsed(SimpleDefinitionFinder,DefinitionSite)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeReturns.java
Original range: 76-120
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if a function result might be used.  A result might be use if:
   * - Function must is exported.
   * - The definition is never accessed outside a function call context.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean callResultsMaybeUsed(
77 |       SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder, DefinitionSite definitionSite) {
78 | 
79 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
80 | 
81 |     // Assume non-function definitions results are used.
82 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
83 |     if (rValue == null || !rValue.isFunction()) {
84 |       return true;
85 |     }
86 | 
87 |     // Be conservative, don't try to optimize any declaration that isn't as
88 |     // simple function declaration or assignment.
89 |     if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isSimpleFunctionDeclaration(rValue)) {
90 |       return true;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     if (!defFinder.canModifyDefinition(definition)) {
94 |       return true;
95 |     }
96 | 
97 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
98 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
99 |       // Assume indirect definitions references use the result
100 |       Node useNodeParent = site.node.getParent();
101 |       if (isCall(site)) {
102 |         Node callNode = useNodeParent;
103 |         Preconditions.checkState(callNode.isCall());
104 |         if (NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(callNode)) {
105 |           return true;
106 |         }
107 |       } else {
108 |         // Allow a standalone name reference.
109 |         //     var a;
110 |         if (!useNodeParent.isVar()) {
111 |           return true;
112 |         }
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Add specialization support.
116 |     }
117 | 
118 |     // No possible use of the definition result
119 |     return false;
120 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.JsFileLineParser.doParse(String,Reader)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/JsFileLineParser.java
Original range: 119-196
Documentation:
/**
   * Performs the line-by-line parsing of the given fileContents. This method
   * strips out Javascript comments and then uses the abstract parseLine()
   * method to do the line parsing.
   *
   * @param filePath The path to the file being parsed. Used for reporting parse
   *     exceptions.
   * @param fileContents A reader for the contents of the file.
   */
Method code:
119 |   void doParse(String filePath, Reader fileContents) {
120 |     this.filePath = filePath;
121 |     parseSucceeded = true;
122 | 
123 |     BufferedReader lineBuffer = new BufferedReader(fileContents);
124 | 
125 |     // Parse all lines.
126 |     String line = null;
127 |     lineNum = 0;
128 |     boolean inMultilineComment = false;
129 | 
130 |     try {
131 |       while (null != (line = lineBuffer.readLine())) {
132 |         ++lineNum;
133 |         try {
134 |           String revisedLine = line;
135 |           if (inMultilineComment) {
136 |             int endOfComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/");
137 |             if (endOfComment != -1) {
138 |               revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(endOfComment + 2);
139 |               inMultilineComment = false;
140 |             } else {
141 |               revisedLine = "";
142 |             }
143 |           }
144 | 
145 |           if (!inMultilineComment) {
146 |             while (true) {
147 |               int startOfLineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("//");
148 |               int startOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("/*");
149 |               if (startOfLineComment != -1 &&
150 |                   (startOfMultilineComment == -1 ||
151 |                    startOfLineComment < startOfMultilineComment)) {
152 |                 revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(0, startOfLineComment);
153 |                 break;
154 |               } else if (startOfMultilineComment != -1) {
155 |                 int endOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/",
156 |                     startOfMultilineComment + 2);
157 |                 if (endOfMultilineComment == -1) {
158 |                   revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(
159 |                       0, startOfMultilineComment);
160 |                   inMultilineComment = true;
161 |                   break;
162 |                 } else {
163 |                   revisedLine =
164 |                       revisedLine.substring(0, startOfMultilineComment) +
165 |                       revisedLine.substring(endOfMultilineComment + 2);
166 |                 }
167 |               } else {
168 |                 break;
169 |               }
170 |             }
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           if (!revisedLine.isEmpty()) {
174 |             // This check for shortcut mode should be redundant, but
175 |             // it's done for safety reasons.
176 |             if (!parseLine(revisedLine) && shortcutMode) {
177 |               break;
178 |             }
179 |           }
180 |         } catch (ParseException e) {
181 |           // Inform the error handler of the exception.
182 |           errorManager.report(
183 |               e.isFatal() ? CheckLevel.ERROR : CheckLevel.WARNING,
184 |               JSError.make(filePath, lineNum, 0 /* char offset */,
185 |                   e.isFatal() ? PARSE_ERROR : PARSE_WARNING,
186 |                   e.getMessage(), line));
187 |           parseSucceeded = parseSucceeded && !e.isFatal();
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (IOException e) {
191 |       errorManager.report(CheckLevel.ERROR,
192 |           JSError.make(filePath, 0, 0 /* char offset */,
193 |               PARSE_ERROR, "Error reading file: " + filePath));
194 |       parseSucceeded = false;
195 |     }
196 |   }

131 |     public int color() {

134 | 
135 |       // Sort nodes by degree.
136 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
137 |         @Override
138 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }
144 |       });
145 | 
146 |       // Idea: From the highest to lowest degree, assign any uncolored node with
147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.
148 |       int count = 0;
149 |       do {
150 |         Color color = new Color(count);
151 |         SubGraph<N, E> subgraph = graph.newSubGraph();
152 |         for (Iterator<GraphNode<N, E>> i = worklist.iterator(); i.hasNext();) {
153 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
154 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
155 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
156 |             node.setAnnotation(color);
157 |             i.remove();
158 |           }
159 |         }
160 |         count++;
161 |       } while (!worklist.isEmpty());
162 |       @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
163 |       N[] map = (N[]) new Object[count];
164 |       colorToNodeMap = map;
165 |       return count;
166 |     }

/**
     * Replaces an assignment like x = {...} with t1=a,t2=b,t3=c,true.
     * Note that the resulting expression will always evaluate to
     * true, as would the x = {...} expression.
     */
Method code:
315 |     private void replaceAssignmentExpression(Var v, Reference ref,
316 |                                              Map<String, String> varmap) {
317 |       // Compute all of the assignments necessary
318 |       List<Node> nodes = Lists.newArrayList();
319 |       Node val = ref.getAssignedValue();
320 |       blacklistVarReferencesInTree(val, v.scope);
321 |       Preconditions.checkState(val.isObjectLit());
322 |       Set<String> all = Sets.newLinkedHashSet(varmap.keySet());
323 |       for (Node key = val.getFirstChild(); key != null;
324 |            key = key.getNext()) {
325 |         String var = key.getString();
326 |         Node value = key.removeFirstChild();
327 |         // TODO(user): Copy type information.
328 |         nodes.add(
329 |             IR.assign(
330 |                 IR.name(varmap.get(var)),
331 |                 value));
332 |         all.remove(var);
333 |       }
334 | 
335 |       // TODO(user): Better source information.
336 |       for (String var : all) {
337 |         nodes.add(
338 |             IR.assign(
339 |                 IR.name(varmap.get(var)),
340 |                 NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(null)));
341 |       }
342 | 
343 |       Node replacement;
344 |       if (nodes.isEmpty()) {
345 |         replacement = IR.trueNode();
346 |       } else {
347 |         // All assignments evaluate to true, so make sure that the
348 |         // expr statement evaluates to true in case it matters.
349 |         nodes.add(IR.trueNode());
350 | 
351 |         // Join these using COMMA.  A COMMA node must have 2 children, so we
352 |         // create a tree. In the tree the first child be the COMMA to match
353 |         // the parser, otherwise tree equality tests fail.
354 |         nodes = Lists.reverse(nodes);
355 |         replacement = new Node(Token.COMMA);
356 |         Node cur = replacement;
357 |         int i;
358 |         for (i = 0; i < nodes.size() - 2; i++) {
359 |           cur.addChildToFront(nodes.get(i));
360 |           Node t = new Node(Token.COMMA);
361 |           cur.addChildToFront(t);
362 |           cur = t;
363 |         }
364 |         cur.addChildToFront(nodes.get(i));
365 |         cur.addChildToFront(nodes.get(i + 1));
366 |       }
367 | 
368 |       Node replace = ref.getParent();
369 |       replacement.copyInformationFromForTree(replace);
370 | 
371 |       if (replace.isVar()) {
372 |         replace.getParent().replaceChild(
373 |             replace, NodeUtil.newExpr(replacement));
374 |       } else {
375 |         replace.getParent().replaceChild(replace, replacement);
376 |       }
377 |     }

===== M1546 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

/**
     * Determines whether the given variable is declared as a constant
     * and may be inlined.
     */
Method code:
454 |     private boolean isInlineableDeclaredConstant(Var var,
455 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
456 |       if (!identifyConstants.apply(var)) {
457 |         return false;
458 |       }
459 | 
460 |       if (!refInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
461 |         return false;
462 |       }
463 | 
464 |       Reference init = refInfo.getInitializingReferenceForConstants();
465 |       if (init == null) {
466 |         return false;
467 |       }
468 | 
469 |       Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
470 |       if (value == null) {
471 |         // This constant is either externally defined or initialized indirectly
472 |         // (e.g. in an function expression used to hide
473 |         // temporary variables), so the constant is ineligible for inlining.
474 |         return false;
475 |       }
476 | 
477 |       // Is the constant's value immutable?
478 |       if (!NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value)) {
479 |         return false;
480 |       }
481 | 
482 |       // Determine if we should really inline a String or not.
483 |       return !value.isString() ||
484 |           isStringWorthInlining(var, refInfo.references);
485 |     }

/**
   * @return an {@link Definition} object if the node contains a definition or
   *     {@code null} otherwise.
   */
Method code:
37 |   static Definition getDefinition(Node n, boolean isExtern) {
38 |     // TODO(user): Since we have parent pointers handy. A lot of constructors
39 |     // can be simplified.
40 | 
41 |     // This logic must match #isDefinitionNode
42 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
43 |     if (parent == null) {
44 |       return null;
45 |     }
46 | 
47 |     if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n) && n.hasChildren()) {
48 |       return new VarDefinition(n, isExtern);
49 |     } else if (parent.isFunction() && parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
50 |       if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
51 |         return new NamedFunctionDefinition(parent, isExtern);
52 |       } else if (!n.getString().equals("")) {
53 |         return new FunctionExpressionDefinition(parent, isExtern);
54 |       }
55 |     } else if (parent.isAssign() && parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
56 |       return new AssignmentDefinition(parent, isExtern);
57 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
58 |       return new ObjectLiteralPropertyDefinition(parent, n, n.getFirstChild(),
59 |           isExtern);
60 |     } else if (parent.isParamList()) {
61 |       Node function = parent.getParent();
62 |       return new FunctionArgumentDefinition(function, n, isExtern);
63 |     }
64 |     return null;
65 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 519-583
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
519 |     private boolean canInline(
520 |         Reference declaration,
521 |         Reference initialization,
522 |         Reference reference) {
523 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
524 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
525 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
526 |         return false;
527 |       }
528 | 
529 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
530 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
531 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
532 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
533 |           !initialization.getGrandparent().isExprResult()) {
534 |         return false;
535 |       }
536 | 
537 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
538 |       // scope boundaries
539 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
540 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
541 |         return false;
542 |       }
543 | 
544 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
545 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
546 |       //   var a = b.c;
547 |       //   a();
548 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
549 |       // rather than the context of the window.
550 |       //   var a = b.c;
551 |       //   f(a)
552 |       // is ok.
553 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
554 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
555 |       if (value.isGetProp()
556 |           && reference.getParent().isCall()
557 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNode()) {
558 |         return false;
559 |       }
560 | 
561 |       if (value.isFunction()) {
562 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
563 |         if (reference.getParent().isCall()) {
564 |           CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
565 |           // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
566 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
567 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
568 |               convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
569 |           if (relationship != null) {
570 |             return false;
571 |           }
572 | 
573 |           // issue 668: Don't inline singleton getter methods
574 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
575 |           if (convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(callNode) != null) {
576 |             return false;
577 |           }
578 |         }
579 |       }
580 | 
581 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
582 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
583 |     }

109 |

115 | 
116 |         case '[':
117 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
118 | 
119 |         case ']':

122 |         case '?':
123 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;

126 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
127 | 
128 |         case ':':
129 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;

132 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;

134 |         case '|':

157 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal traversal, Node node, Node parent) {
158 |       // Arguments of external functions should not count as name
159 |       // definitions.  They are placeholder names for documentation

161 |       if (inExterns && node.isName() && parent.isParamList()) {
162 |         return;
163 |       }
164 | 
165 |       Definition def =
166 |           DefinitionsRemover.getDefinition(node, inExterns);

168 |         String name = getSimplifiedName(def.getLValue());
169 |         if (name != null) {

171 |           if ((rValue != null) &&
172 |               !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(rValue) &&
173 |               !rValue.isFunction()) {
174 |

182 |           // illegal to have untyped stubs in the externs definitions.

184 |             // We need special handling of untyped externs stubs here:
185 |             //    the stub should be dropped if the name is provided elsewhere.
186 | 
187 |             List<Definition> stubsToRemove = Lists.newArrayList();

192 |             // literal key.

195 |                 if (prevDef instanceof ExternalNameOnlyDefinition

197 |                   String prevName = prevDef.getLValue().getQualifiedName();

199 |                     // Drop this stub, there is a real definition.
200 |                     stubsToRemove.add(prevDef);
201 |                   }
202 |                 }
203 |               }
204 | 
205 |               for (Definition prevDef : stubsToRemove) {
206 |                 nameDefinitionMultimap.remove(name, prevDef);
207 |               }
208 |             }
209 |           }
210 |

212 |           definitionSiteMap.put(node,
213 |                                 new DefinitionSite(node,
214 |                                                    def,

===== M1601 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 177-289
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
177 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
178 | 
179 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
180 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.isParamList());
181 | 
182 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
183 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
184 |     boolean changed = false;
185 | 
186 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
187 |     // array.
188 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
189 | 
190 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
191 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
192 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
193 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
194 | 
195 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
196 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
197 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
198 | 
199 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
200 | 
201 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
202 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
203 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
204 |       if (!getElem.isGetElem()) {
205 |         return false;
206 |       }
207 | 
208 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
209 | 
210 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
211 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
212 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
213 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
214 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
215 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
216 |         // it is never 'callee'.
217 |         return false; // Give up.
218 |       }
219 | 
220 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
221 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
222 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
223 |       if (getElemParent.isCall() &&
224 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
225 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
226 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
227 |         return false;
228 |       }
229 | 
230 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
231 |       // than all the one we saw before.
232 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
233 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
234 |         highestIndex = value;
235 |       }
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
239 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
240 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
241 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
242 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
243 | 
244 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
245 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
246 | 
247 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
248 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
249 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
250 |       String name = getNewName();
251 |       argNames[i] = name;
252 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(IR.name(name));
253 |       changed = true;
254 |     }
255 | 
256 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
257 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
258 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
259 | 
260 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
261 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
262 |         continue;
263 |       }
264 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
265 | 
266 |       // Unnamed parameter.
267 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
268 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
269 |             IR.name(argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
270 |       } else {
271 | 
272 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
273 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
274 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
275 | 
276 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
277 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
278 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
279 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
280 |           name = name.getNext();
281 |         }
282 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
283 |             IR.name(name.getString()));
284 |       }
285 |       changed = true;
286 |     }
287 | 
288 |     return changed;
289 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionRewriter.java
Original range: 57-104
Documentation:

Method code:
57 |   @Override
58 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
59 |     List<Reducer> reducers = ImmutableList.of(new ReturnConstantReducer(),
60 |                                               new GetterReducer(),
61 |                                               new SetterReducer(),
62 |                                               new EmptyFunctionReducer(),
63 |                                               new IdentityReducer());
64 | 
65 |     Multimap<Reducer, Reduction> reductionMap = HashMultimap.create();
66 | 
67 |     // Accumulate possible reductions in the reduction multi map.  They
68 |     // will be applied in the loop below.
69 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root,
70 |                            new ReductionGatherer(reducers, reductionMap));
71 | 
72 |     // Apply reductions iff they will provide some savings.
73 |     for (Reducer reducer : reducers) {
74 |       Collection<Reduction> reductions = reductionMap.get(reducer);
75 |       if (reductions.isEmpty()) {
76 |         continue;
77 |       }
78 | 
79 |       Node helperCode = parseHelperCode(reducer);
80 |       if (helperCode == null) {
81 |         continue;
82 |       }
83 | 
84 |       int helperCodeCost = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(helperCode);
85 | 
86 |       // Estimate savings
87 |       int savings = 0;
88 |       for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
89 |         savings += reduction.estimateSavings();
90 |       }
91 | 
92 |       // Compare estimated savings against the helper cost.  Apply
93 |       // reductions if doing so will result in some savings.
94 |       if (savings > (helperCodeCost + SAVINGS_THRESHOLD)) {
95 |         for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
96 |           reduction.apply();
97 |         }
98 | 
99 |         Node addingRoot = compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(null);
100 |         addingRoot.addChildrenToFront(helperCode);
101 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
102 |       }
103 |     }
104 |   }

84 |   public JSModuleGraph(List<JSModule> modulesInDepOrder) {
85 |     Preconditions.checkState(
86 |         modulesInDepOrder.size() == Sets.newHashSet(modulesInDepOrder).size(),
87 |         "Found duplicate modules");
88 |     modules = ImmutableList.copyOf(modulesInDepOrder);

102 |       }

105 |       if (depth == modulesByDepth.size()) {
106 |         modulesByDepth.add(new ArrayList<JSModule>());
107 |       }

Method code:
175 |     @Override
176 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
177 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
178 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
179 |         return;
180 |       }
181 | 
182 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
183 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
184 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
189 |         Var var = vars.next();
190 | 
191 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
192 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
193 |           continue;
194 |         }
195 | 
196 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
197 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
198 |           continue;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
202 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
203 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
204 |           continue;
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
208 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
209 | 
210 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
211 |         // shadowed variable.
212 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
213 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
214 |         }
215 | 
216 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
217 | 
218 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
219 |           String targetPseudoName =
220 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
221 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
222 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 76-116
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a expression. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   * Note: unlike getBooleanValue this function does not return UNKNOWN
   * for expressions with side-effects.
   */
Method code:
76 |   static TernaryValue getImpureBooleanValue(Node n) {
77 |     switch (n.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
79 |       case Token.COMMA:
80 |         // For ASSIGN and COMMA the value is the value of the RHS.
81 |         return getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
82 |       case Token.NOT:
83 |         TernaryValue value = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
84 |         return value.not();
85 |       case Token.AND: {
86 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
87 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
88 |         return lhs.and(rhs);
89 |       }
90 |       case Token.OR:  {
91 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
92 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
93 |         return lhs.or(rhs);
94 |       }
95 |       case Token.HOOK:  {
96 |         TernaryValue trueValue = getImpureBooleanValue(
97 |             n.getFirstChild().getNext());
98 |         TernaryValue falseValue = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
99 |         if (trueValue.equals(falseValue)) {
100 |           return trueValue;
101 |         } else {
102 |           return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
103 |         }
104 |       }
105 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
106 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
107 |         // ignoring side-effects
108 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
109 | 
110 |       case Token.VOID:
111 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
112 | 
113 |       default:
114 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n);
115 |     }
116 |   }

===== M1673 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 130-179
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to remove n if an unconditional branch node (break, continue or
   * return) if the target of n is the same as the the follow of n. That is, if
   * we remove n, the control flow remains the same. Also if n targets to
   * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
   * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
   * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
   *
   * break -> break -> break
   *
   * where all 3 break's are useless. The order of removal matters. When we
   * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
   * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
   * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
   *
   * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
   *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
   */
Method code:
130 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
131 |   private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
132 |     /*
133 |      * For each of the unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
134 |      * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
135 |      * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
136 |      *
137 |      * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
138 |      * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
139 |      * much nicer.
140 |      */
141 | 
142 |     // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
143 |     if (n == null) {
144 |        return n;
145 |     }
146 | 
147 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = curCfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
148 | 
149 |     if (gNode == null) {
150 |       return n;
151 |     }
152 | 
153 |     switch (n.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.RETURN:
155 |         if (n.hasChildren()) {
156 |           break;
157 |         }
158 |       case Token.BREAK:
159 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
160 | 
161 |         // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
162 |         // branches to the same node. If removing it the control flow still
163 |         // branches to that same node. It is safe to remove it.
164 |         List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
165 |         if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
166 |             // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
167 |             (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
168 | 
169 |           Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
170 |           Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
171 |           Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
172 |           if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
173 |             removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
174 |             return fallThrough;
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |     }
178 |     return n;
179 |   }

/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block, n);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child, n);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }
178 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1120-1300

/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1120 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1121 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1122 | 
1123 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1124 |       case Token.NOT:
1125 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1126 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1127 |           case Token.NOT: {
1128 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1129 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1130 |               reportCodeChange();
1131 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1132 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1133 |               return newRoot;
1134 |             }
1135 |           case Token.AND:
1136 |           case Token.OR: {
1137 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1138 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1139 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1140 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1141 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1142 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1143 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1144 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1145 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1146 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1147 |               Node left, right;
1148 | 
1149 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1150 |               // due to the added ()
1151 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1152 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1153 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1154 |                 // If an expression has higher precendence than && or ||,
1155 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1156 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1157 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1158 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1159 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1160 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1161 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1162 |                   return n;
1163 |                 }
1164 |               }
1165 | 
1166 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1167 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1168 |               } else {
1169 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1170 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1171 |               }
1172 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1173 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1174 |               } else {
1175 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1176 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1177 |               }
1178 | 
1179 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1180 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1181 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1182 |               reportCodeChange();
1183 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1184 |               // AND and OR children below.
1185 |               return newRoot;
1186 |             }
1187 | 
1188 |            default:
1189 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1190 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1191 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1192 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1193 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1194 |              }
1195 |         }
1196 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1197 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1198 |         return n;
1199 | 
1200 |       case Token.OR:
1201 |       case Token.AND: {
1202 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1203 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1204 | 
1205 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1206 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1207 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1208 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1209 | 
1210 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1211 |         // Handle four cases:
1212 |         //   x || false --> x
1213 |         //   x || true  --> true
1214 |         //   x && true --> x
1215 |         //   x && false  --> false
1216 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1217 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1218 |           int type = n.getType();
1219 |           Node replacement = null;
1220 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1221 | 
1222 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1223 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1224 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1225 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1226 |             replacement = left;
1227 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1228 |             replacement = right;
1229 |           }
1230 | 
1231 |           if (replacement != null) {
1232 |             n.detachChildren();
1233 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1234 |             reportCodeChange();
1235 |             return replacement;
1236 |           }
1237 |         }
1238 |         return n;
1239 |       }
1240 | 
1241 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1242 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1243 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1244 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1245 | 
1246 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1247 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1248 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1249 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1250 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1251 | 
1252 |         // Handle four cases:
1253 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1254 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1255 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1256 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1257 |         Node replacement = null;
1258 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1259 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1260 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1261 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1262 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1263 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1264 |           replacement = condition;
1265 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1266 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1267 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1268 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1269 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1270 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1271 |           // Remove useless true case.
1272 |           n.detachChildren();
1273 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1274 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1275 |           // Remove useless false case
1276 |           n.detachChildren();
1277 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1278 |         }
1279 | 
1280 |         if (replacement != null) {
1281 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1282 |           n = replacement;
1283 |           reportCodeChange();
1284 |         }
1285 | 
1286 |         return n;
1287 |       }
1288 | 
1289 |       default:
1290 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1291 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1292 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1293 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1294 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1295 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1296 |         }
1297 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1298 |         return n;
1299 |     }
1300 |   }

/**
   * Hoists inputs with the @externs annotation into the externs list.
   */
Method code:
1364 |   private void hoistExterns(Node externsRoot) {
1365 |     boolean staleInputs = false;
1366 |     for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1367 |       if (options.dependencyOptions.needsManagement() &&
1368 |           options.closurePass) {
1369 |         // If we're doing scanning dependency info anyway, use that
1370 |         // information to skip sources that obviously aren't externs.
1371 |         if (!input.getProvides().isEmpty() || !input.getRequires().isEmpty()) {
1372 |           continue;
1373 |         }
1374 |       }
1375 | 
1376 |       Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1377 | 
1378 |       // Inputs can have a null AST on a parse error.
1379 |       if (n == null) {
1380 |         continue;
1381 |       }
1382 | 
1383 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1384 |       if (info != null && info.isExterns()) {
1385 |         // If the input file is explicitly marked as an externs file, then
1386 |         // assume the programmer made a mistake and throw it into
1387 |         // the externs pile anyways.
1388 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1389 |         input.setIsExtern(true);
1390 | 
1391 |         input.getModule().remove(input);
1392 | 
1393 |         externs.add(input);
1394 |         staleInputs = true;
1395 |       }
1396 |     }
1397 | 
1398 |     if (staleInputs) {
1399 |       repartitionInputs();
1400 |     }
1401 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ScopedAliases.hotSwapScript(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ScopedAliases.java
Original range: 103-142
Documentation:

Method code:
103 |   @Override
104 |   public void hotSwapScript(Node root, Node originalRoot) {
105 |     Traversal traversal = new Traversal();
106 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, traversal);
107 | 
108 |     if (!traversal.hasErrors()) {
109 | 
110 |       // Apply the aliases.
111 |       for (AliasUsage aliasUsage : traversal.getAliasUsages()) {
112 |         aliasUsage.applyAlias();
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       // Remove the alias definitions.
116 |       for (Node aliasDefinition : traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder()) {
117 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().isVar() &&
118 |             aliasDefinition.getParent().hasOneChild()) {
119 |           aliasDefinition.getParent().detachFromParent();
120 |         } else {
121 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       // Collapse the scopes.
126 |       for (Node scopeCall : traversal.getScopeCalls()) {
127 |         Node expressionWithScopeCall = scopeCall.getParent();
128 |         Node scopeClosureBlock = scopeCall.getLastChild().getLastChild();
129 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();
130 |         expressionWithScopeCall.getParent().replaceChild(
131 |             expressionWithScopeCall,
132 |             scopeClosureBlock);
133 |         NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(scopeClosureBlock);
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       if (traversal.getAliasUsages().size() > 0 ||
137 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder().size() > 0 ||
138 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
139 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 |   }

===== M1753 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.Candidate.canInline()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.java
Original range: 255-375
Documentation:

Method code:
255 |     private boolean canInline() {
256 | 
257 |       // Cannot inline a parameter.
258 |       if (defCfgNode.isFunction()) {
259 |         return false;
260 |       }
261 | 
262 |       getDefinition(defCfgNode, null);
263 |       getNumUseInUseCfgNode(useCfgNode, null);
264 | 
265 |       // Definition was not found.
266 |       if (def == null) {
267 |         return false;
268 |       }
269 | 
270 |       // Check that the assignment isn't used as a R-Value.
271 |       // TODO(user): Certain cases we can still inline.
272 |       if (def.isAssign() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(def.getParent())) {
273 |         return false;
274 |       }
275 | 
276 | 
277 |       // The right of the definition has side effect:
278 |       // Example, for x:
279 |       // x = readProp(b), modifyProp(b); print(x);
280 |       if (checkRightOf(def, defCfgNode, SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE)) {
281 |         return false;
282 |       }
283 | 
284 |       // Similar check as the above but this time, all the sub-expressions
285 |       // left of the use of the variable.
286 |       // x = readProp(b); modifyProp(b), print(x);
287 |       if (checkLeftOf(use, useCfgNode, SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE)) {
288 |         return false;
289 |       }
290 | 
291 | 
292 |       // TODO(user): Side-effect is ok sometimes. As long as there are no
293 |       // side-effect function down all paths to the use. Once we have all the
294 |       // side-effect analysis tool.
295 |       if (NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(def.getLastChild())) {
296 |         return false;
297 |       }
298 | 
299 |       // TODO(user): We could inline all the uses if the expression is short.
300 | 
301 |       // Finally we have to make sure that there are no more than one use
302 |       // in the program and in the CFG node. Even when it is semantically
303 |       // correctly inlining twice increases code size.
304 |       if (numUseWithinUseCfgNode != 1) {
305 |         return false;
306 |       }
307 | 
308 |       // Make sure that the name is not within a loop
309 |       if (NodeUtil.isWithinLoop(use)) {
310 |         return false;
311 |       }
312 | 
313 | 
314 |       Collection<Node> uses = reachingUses.getUses(varName, defCfgNode);
315 | 
316 |       if (uses.size() != 1) {
317 |         return false;
318 |       }
319 | 
320 |       // We give up inling stuff with R-Value that has GETPROP, GETELEM,
321 |       // or anything that creates a new object.
322 |       // Example:
323 |       // var x = a.b.c; j.c = 1; print(x);
324 |       // Inlining print(a.b.c) is not safe consider j and be alias to a.b.
325 |       // TODO(user): We could get more accuracy by looking more in-detail
326 |       // what j is and what x is trying to into to.
327 |       if (NodeUtil.has(def.getLastChild(),
328 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
329 |               @Override
330 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
331 |                 switch (input.getType()) {
332 |                   case Token.GETELEM:
333 |                   case Token.GETPROP:
334 |                   case Token.ARRAYLIT:
335 |                   case Token.OBJECTLIT:
336 |                   case Token.REGEXP:
337 |                   case Token.NEW:
338 |                     return true;
339 |                 }
340 |                 return false;
341 |               }
342 |           },
343 |           new Predicate<Node>() {
344 |               @Override
345 |               public boolean apply(Node input) {
346 |                 // Recurse if the node is not a function.
347 |                 return !input.isFunction();
348 |               }
349 |           })) {
350 |         return false;
351 |       }
352 | 
353 |       // We can skip the side effect check along the paths of two nodes if
354 |       // they are just next to each other.
355 |       if (NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(defCfgNode.getParent()) &&
356 |           defCfgNode.getNext() != useCfgNode) {
357 |         // Similar side effect check as above but this time the side effect is
358 |         // else where along the path.
359 |         // x = readProp(b); while(modifyProp(b)) {}; print(x);
360 |         CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>
361 |           pathCheck = new CheckPathsBetweenNodes<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>(
362 |                  cfg,
363 |                  cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(defCfgNode),
364 |                  cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(useCfgNode),
365 |                  SIDE_EFFECT_PREDICATE,
366 |                  Predicates.
367 |                      <DiGraphEdge<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>>alwaysTrue(),
368 |                  false);
369 |         if (pathCheck.somePathsSatisfyPredicate()) {
370 |           return false;
371 |         }
372 |       }
373 | 
374 |       return true;
375 |     }

   * Traverses a function, which creates a new scope in javascript.
   *
   * Note that CATCH blocks also create a new scope, but only for the
   * catch variable. Declarations within the block actually belong to the

639 |   private void handleReturn(Node node) {

642 |       Node curHandler = iter.next();

986 |         sb.append(": ");
987 |         String value;

989 |           default:

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get
   * JsDoc descriptions.
   * @return Whether we found a type annotation.
   */
Method code:
2344 |   private boolean lookAheadForTypeAnnotation() {
2345 |     boolean matchedLc = false;
2346 |     int c;
2347 |     while (true) {
2348 |       c = stream.getChar();
2349 |       if (c == ' ') {
2350 |         continue;
2351 |       } else if (c == '{') {
2352 |         matchedLc = true;
2353 |         break;
2354 |       } else {
2355 |         break;
2356 |       }
2357 |     }
2358 |     stream.ungetChar(c);
2359 |     return matchedLc;
2360 |   }

/**
   * We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
   * very deeply nested operators and run out of stack space, so we
   * just unroll the recursion when possible.
   *
   * We assume nodes are left-recursive.
   */
Method code:
741 |   private void unrollBinaryOperator(
742 |       Node n, int op, String opStr, Context context,
743 |       Context rhsContext, int leftPrecedence, int rightPrecedence) {
744 |     Node firstNonOperator = n.getFirstChild();
745 |     while (firstNonOperator.getType() == op) {
746 |       firstNonOperator = firstNonOperator.getFirstChild();
747 |     }
748 | 
749 |     addExpr(firstNonOperator, leftPrecedence, context);
750 | 
751 |     Node current = firstNonOperator;
752 |     do {
753 |       current = current.getParent();
754 |       cc.addOp(opStr, true);
755 |       addExpr(current.getFirstChild().getNext(), rightPrecedence, rhsContext);
756 |     } while (current != n);
757 |   }

/**
   * Parses the externs and main inputs.
   *
   * @return A synthetic root node whose two children are the externs root
   *     and the main root
