Method code:
1236 |   Node parseInputs() {
1237 |     boolean devMode = options.devMode != DevMode.OFF;
1238 | 
1239 |     // If old roots exist (we are parsing a second time), detach each of the
1240 |     // individual file parse trees.
1241 |     if (externsRoot != null) {
1242 |       externsRoot.detachChildren();
1243 |     }
1244 |     if (jsRoot != null) {
1245 |       jsRoot.detachChildren();
1246 |     }
1247 | 
1248 |     // Parse main js sources.
1249 |     jsRoot = IR.block();
1250 |     jsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1251 | 
1252 |     externsRoot = IR.block();
1253 |     externsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1254 | 
1255 |     externAndJsRoot = IR.block(externsRoot, jsRoot);
1256 |     externAndJsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1257 | 
1258 |     if (options.tracer.isOn()) {
1259 |       tracker = new PerformanceTracker(jsRoot, options.tracer);
1260 |       addChangeHandler(tracker.getCodeChangeHandler());
1261 |     }
1262 | 
1263 |     Tracer tracer = newTracer("parseInputs");
1264 | 
1265 |     try {
1266 |       // Parse externs sources.
1267 |       for (CompilerInput input : externs) {
1268 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1269 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1270 |           return null;
1271 |         }
1272 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1273 |       }
1274 | 
1275 |       // Modules inferred in ProcessCommonJS pass.
1276 |       if (options.transformAMDToCJSModules || options.processCommonJSModules) {
1277 |         processAMDAndCommonJSModules();
1278 |       }
1279 | 
1280 |       hoistExterns(externsRoot);
1281 | 
1282 |       // Check if the sources need to be re-ordered.
1283 |       boolean staleInputs = false;
1284 |       if (options.dependencyOptions.needsManagement() &&
1285 |           options.closurePass) {
1286 |         for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1287 |           // Forward-declare all the provided types, so that they
1288 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1289 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1290 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1291 |           }
1292 |         }
1293 | 
1294 |         try {
1295 |           inputs =
1296 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1297 |               .manageDependencies(options.dependencyOptions, inputs);
1298 |           staleInputs = true;
1299 |         } catch (CircularDependencyException e) {
1300 |           report(JSError.make(
1301 |               JSModule.CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1302 | 
1303 |           // If in IDE mode, we ignore the error and keep going.
1304 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1305 |             return null;
1306 |           }
1307 |         } catch (MissingProvideException e) {
1308 |           report(JSError.make(
1309 |               MISSING_ENTRY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1310 | 
1311 |           // If in IDE mode, we ignore the error and keep going.
1312 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1313 |             return null;
1314 |           }
1315 |         }
1316 |       }
1317 | 
1318 |       hoistNoCompileFiles();
1319 | 
1320 |       if (staleInputs) {
1321 |         repartitionInputs();
1322 |       }
1323 | 
1324 |       // Build the AST.
1325 |       for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1326 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1327 |         if (n == null) {
1328 |           continue;
1329 |         }
1330 | 
1331 |         if (devMode) {
1332 |           runSanityCheck();
1333 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1334 |             return null;
1335 |           }
1336 |         }
1337 | 
1338 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null ||
1339 |             options.nameReferenceReportPath != null) {
1340 | 
1341 |           // Annotate the nodes in the tree with information from the
1342 |           // input file. This information is used to construct the SourceMap.
1343 |           SourceInformationAnnotator sia =
1344 |               new SourceInformationAnnotator(
1345 |                   input.getName(), options.devMode != DevMode.OFF);
1346 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(this, n, sia);
1347 |         }
1348 | 
1349 |         jsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1350 |       }
1351 | 
1352 |       if (hasErrors()) {
1353 |         return null;
1354 |       }
1355 |       return externAndJsRoot;
1356 |     } finally {

1358 |     }
1359 |   }

152 |   @Override
153 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
154 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
155 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
156 | 
157 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
158 |     boolean conditional = false;

===== M1849 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedClassProperties.isPinningPropertyUse(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedClassProperties.java
Original range: 119-143
Documentation:
/**
   * @return Whether the property is used in a way that prevents its removal.
   */
Method code:
119 |   private boolean isPinningPropertyUse(Node n) {
120 |     // Rather than looking for cases that are uses, we assume all references are
121 |     // pinning uses unless they are:
122 |     //  - a simple assignment (x.a = 1)
123 |     //  - a compound assignment or increment (x++, x += 1) whose result is
124 |     //    otherwise unused
125 | 
126 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
127 |     if (n == parent.getFirstChild()) {
128 |       if (parent.isAssign()) {
129 |         // A simple assignment doesn't pin the property.
130 |         return false;
131 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent)
132 |             || parent.isInc() || parent.isDec()) {
133 |         // In general, compound assignments are both reads and writes, but
134 |         // if the property is never otherwise read we can consider it simply
135 |         // a write.
136 |         // However if the assign expression is used as part of a larger
137 |         // expression, we much consider it a read. For example:
138 |         //    x = (y.a += 1);
139 |         return NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 |     return true;
143 |   }

307 |       // If we are traversing the externs, then we save a pointer to the scope
308 |       // generated by them, so that we can do lookups in it later.
309 |       if (externsRoot != null && n == externsRoot) {
310 |         externsScope = t.getScope();
311 |       }
312 | 
313 |       String name;
314 |       boolean isSet = false;
315 |       Name.Type type = Name.Type.OTHER;
316 |       boolean isPropAssign = false;
317 | 
318 |       switch (n.getType()) {
319 |         case Token.GETTER_DEF:
320 |         case Token.SETTER_DEF:
321 |         case Token.STRING_KEY:
322 |           // This may be a key in an object literal declaration.
323 |           name = null;
324 |           if (parent != null && parent.isObjectLit()) {
325 |             name = getNameForObjLitKey(n);
326 |           }
327 |           if (name == null) return;
328 |           isSet = true;
329 |           switch (n.getType()) {
330 |             case Token.STRING_KEY:
331 |               type = getValueType(n.getFirstChild());
332 |               break;
333 |             case Token.GETTER_DEF:
334 |               type = Name.Type.GET;
335 |               break;
336 |             case Token.SETTER_DEF:
337 |               type = Name.Type.SET;
338 |               break;
339 |             default:
340 |               throw new IllegalStateException("unexpected:" + n);
341 |           }
342 |           break;
343 |         case Token.NAME:
344 |           // This may be a variable get or set.
345 |           if (parent != null) {
346 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
347 |               case Token.VAR:
348 |                 isSet = true;
349 |                 Node rvalue = n.getFirstChild();
350 |                 type = rvalue == null ? Name.Type.OTHER : getValueType(rvalue);
351 |                 break;
352 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
353 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
354 |                   isSet = true;
355 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
356 |                 }
357 |                 break;
358 |               case Token.GETPROP:
359 |                 return;
360 |               case Token.FUNCTION:
361 |                 Node gramps = parent.getParent();
362 |                 if (gramps == null ||
363 |                     NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) return;
364 |                 isSet = true;
365 |                 type = Name.Type.FUNCTION;
366 |                 break;
367 |               case Token.INC:
368 |               case Token.DEC:
369 |                 isSet = true;
370 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
371 |                 break;
372 |               default:
373 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
374 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
375 |                   isSet = true;
376 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
377 |                 }
378 |             }
379 |           }
380 |           name = n.getString();
381 |           break;
382 |         case Token.GETPROP:
383 |           // This may be a namespaced name get or set.
384 |           if (parent != null) {
385 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
386 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
387 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
388 |                   isSet = true;
389 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
390 |                   isPropAssign = true;
391 |                 }
392 |                 break;
393 |               case Token.INC:
394 |               case Token.DEC:
395 |                 isSet = true;
396 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
397 |                 break;
398 |               case Token.GETPROP:
399 |                 return;
400 |               default:
401 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
402 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
403 |                   isSet = true;
404 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
405 |                 }
406 |             }
407 |           }
408 |           name = n.getQualifiedName();
409 |           if (name == null) return;
410 |           break;
411 |         default:
412 |           return;
413 |       }
414 | 
415 |       // We are only interested in global names.
416 |       Scope scope = t.getScope();
417 |       if (!isGlobalNameReference(name, scope)) {
418 |         return;
419 |       }
420 | 
421 |       if (isSet) {
422 |         if (isGlobalScope(scope)) {
423 |           handleSetFromGlobal(t, n, parent, name, isPropAssign, type);
424 |         } else {
425 |           handleSetFromLocal(t, n, parent, name);
426 |         }
427 |       } else {
428 |         handleGet(t, n, parent, name);
429 |       }
430 |     }

   * Try to fold a AND/OR node.
   */
Method code:
562 |   private Node tryFoldAndOr(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
563 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
564 | 
565 |     Node result = null;
566 | 
567 |     int type = n.getType();
568 | 
569 |     TernaryValue leftVal = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(left);
570 | 
571 |     if (leftVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
572 |       boolean lval = leftVal.toBoolean(true);
573 | 
574 |       // (TRUE || x) => TRUE (also, (3 || x) => 3)
575 |       // (FALSE && x) => FALSE
576 |       if (lval && type == Token.OR ||
577 |           !lval && type == Token.AND) {
578 |         result = left;
579 | 
580 |       } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
581 |         // (FALSE || x) => x
582 |         // (TRUE && x) => x
583 |         result = right;
584 |       }
585 |     }
586 | 
587 |     // Note: Right hand side folding is handled by
588 |     // PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax#tryMinimizeCondition
589 | 
590 |     if (result != null) {
591 |       // Fold it!
592 |       n.removeChild(result);
593 |       parent.replaceChild(n, result);
594 |       reportCodeChange();
595 | 
596 |       return result;
597 |     } else {
598 |       return n;
599 |     }
600 |   }

   * Returns true if this is an immutable value.

Method code:
490 |   static boolean isImmutableValue(Node n) {
491 |     switch (n.getType()) {
492 |       case Token.STRING:
493 |       case Token.NUMBER:
494 |       case Token.NULL:
495 |       case Token.TRUE:
496 |       case Token.FALSE:
497 |         return true;

120 |   @Override
121 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
122 |     new NodeTraversal(
123 |         compiler, new NormalizeStatements(compiler, assertOnChange))
124 |         .traverseRoots(externs, root);
125 |     if (MAKE_LOCAL_NAMES_UNIQUE) {
126 |       MakeDeclaredNamesUnique renamer = new MakeDeclaredNamesUnique();
127 |       NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, renamer);
128 |       t.traverseRoots(externs, root);
129 |     }
130 |     // It is important that removeDuplicateDeclarations runs after
131 |     // MakeDeclaredNamesUnique in order for catch block exception names to be
132 |     // handled properly. Specifically, catch block exception names are
133 |     // only valid within the catch block, but our currect Scope logic
134 |     // has no concept of this and includes it in the containing function
135 |     // (or global scope). MakeDeclaredNamesUnique makes the catch exception
136 |     // names unique so that removeDuplicateDeclarations() will properly handle
137 |     // cases where a function scope variable conflict with a exception name:
138 |     //   function f() {
139 |     //      try {throw 0;} catch(e) {e; /* catch scope 'e'*/}
140 |     //      var e = 1; // f scope 'e'
141 |     //   }
142 |     // otherwise 'var e = 1' would be rewritten as 'e = 1'.
143 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Introduce a seperate scope for catch nodes.
144 |     removeDuplicateDeclarations(externs, root);
145 |     new PropagateConstantAnnotationsOverVars(compiler, assertOnChange)
146 |         .process(externs, root);
147 | 
148 |     FindExposeAnnotations findExposeAnnotations = new FindExposeAnnotations();
149 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, findExposeAnnotations);
150 |     if (!findExposeAnnotations.exposedProperties.isEmpty()) {
151 |       NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root,
152 |           new RewriteExposedProperties(
153 |               findExposeAnnotations.exposedProperties));
154 |     }
155 | 
156 |     if (!compiler.getLifeCycleStage().isNormalized()) {
157 |       compiler.setLifeCycleStage(LifeCycleStage.NORMALIZED);
158 |     }
159 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.FindDependencyScopes.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Method code:
508 |     @Override
509 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
510 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope()) {
511 |         return;
512 |       }
513 | 
514 |       if (n.isAssign()) {
515 |         Node nameNode = n.getFirstChild();
516 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, nameNode, n);
517 |         if (ns != null) {
518 |           if (parent.isFor() && !NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
519 |             // Patch for assignments that appear in the init,
520 |             // condition or iteration part of a FOR loop.  Without
521 |             // this change, all 3 of those parts try to claim the for
522 |             // loop as their dependency scope.  The last assignment in
523 |             // those three fields wins, which can result in incorrect
524 |             // reference edges between referenced and assigned variables.
525 |             //
526 |             // TODO(user) revisit the dependency scope calculation
527 |             // logic.
528 |             if (parent.getFirstChild().getNext() != n) {
529 |               recordDepScope(n, ns);
530 |             } else {
531 |               recordDepScope(nameNode, ns);
532 |             }
533 |           } else {
534 |             recordDepScope(n, ns);
535 |           }
536 |         }
537 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n)) {
538 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, n, parent);
539 |         recordDepScope(n, ns);
540 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
541 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, n.getFirstChild(), n);
542 |         recordDepScope(n, ns);
543 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isExprCall(n)) {
544 |         Node callNode = n.getFirstChild();
545 |         Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
546 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, nameNode, callNode);
547 |         if (ns != null && ns.onlyAffectsClassDef) {
548 |           recordDepScope(n, ns);
549 |         }
550 |       }
551 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.isCollapsibleValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 76-91
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented  setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is ok for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().isThis();
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

===== M1920 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.GatherReferenceInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 129-169
Documentation:

Method code:
129 |     @Override
130 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
131 |       // Skipping over non-name nodes and empty function names.
132 |       if (!NodeUtil.isReferenceName(n)) {
133 |         return;
134 |       }
135 | 
136 |       // We focus on shadowing local variables as their name occurs much more
137 |       // than global names.
138 |       // TODO(user): Alternatively, we could experiment with using a local
139 |       // name to shadow a global variable.
140 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
141 |         return;
142 |       }
143 | 
144 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
145 |       if (var == null) {
146 |         // extern name or undefined name.
147 |         return;
148 |       }
149 | 
150 |       if (var.getScope().isGlobal()) {
151 |         // We will not shadow a global variable name.
152 |         return;
153 |       }
154 | 
155 |       // Using the definition of upward referencing, fill in the map.
156 |       if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()) {
157 |         for (Scope s = t.getScope();
158 |             s != var.getScope() && s.isLocal(); s = s.getParent()) {
159 |           scopeUpRefMap.put(s.getRootNode(), var.name);
160 |         }
161 |       }
162 | 
163 |       if (var.getScope() == t.getScope()) {
164 |         scopeUpRefMap.put(t.getScopeRoot(), var.name);
165 |       }
166 | 
167 |       // Find in the usage map that tracks a var and all of its usage.
168 |       varToNameUsage.put(var, n);
169 |     }

===== M1921 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.compileInternal()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 660-705
Documentation:

Method code:
660 |   private void compileInternal() {
661 |     setProgress(0.0);
662 |     parse();
663 |     // 15 percent of the work is assumed to be for parsing (based on some
664 |     // minimal analysis on big JS projects, of course this depends on options)
665 |     setProgress(0.15);
666 |     if (hasErrors()) {
667 |       return;
668 |     }
669 | 
670 |     if (!precheck()) {
671 |       return;
672 |     }
673 | 
674 |     if (options.nameAnonymousFunctionsOnly) {
675 |       // TODO(nicksantos): Move this into an instrument() phase maybe?
676 |       check();
677 |       return;
678 |     }
679 | 
680 |     if (!options.skipAllPasses) {
681 |       check();
682 |       if (hasErrors()) {
683 |         return;
684 |       }
685 | 
686 |       if (options.isExternExportsEnabled()
687 |           || options.externExportsPath != null) {
688 |         externExports();
689 |       }
690 | 
691 |       // IDE-mode is defined to stop here, before the heavy rewriting begins.
692 |       if (!options.ideMode) {
693 |         optimize();
694 |       }
695 |     }
696 | 
697 |     if (options.recordFunctionInformation) {
698 |       recordFunctionInformation();
699 |     }
700 | 
701 |     if (options.devMode == DevMode.START_AND_END) {
702 |       runSanityCheck();
703 |     }
704 |     setProgress(1.0);
705 |   }

===== M1956 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 445-496
Documentation:
/**
   * Replace duplicate exits in control structures.  If the node following
   * the exit node expression has the same effect as exit node, the node can
   * be replaced or removed.
   * For example:
   *   "while (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "while (a) {break} return f();"
   *   "while (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "while (a) {break} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
445 |   private Node tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node n) {
446 |     Node result = n.getFirstChild();
447 | 
448 |     // Find the enclosing control structure, if any, that a "break" would exit
449 |     // from.
450 |     Node breakTarget = n;
451 |     for (;!ControlFlowAnalysis.isBreakTarget(breakTarget, null /* no label */);
452 |         breakTarget = breakTarget.getParent()) {
453 |       if (breakTarget.isFunction() || breakTarget.isScript()) {
454 |         // No break target.
455 |         return n;
456 |       }
457 |     }
458 | 
459 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(breakTarget);
460 | 
461 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the break and return will
462 |     // also trigger all the finally blocks. However, the order of execution is
463 |     // slightly changed. Consider:
464 |     //
465 |     // return a() -> finally { b() } -> return a()
466 |     //
467 |     // which would call a() first. However, changing the first return to a
468 |     // break will result in calling b().
469 | 
470 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
471 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
472 | 
473 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
474 |       // There were finally clauses
475 |       if (!isPure(result)) {
476 |         // Can't defer the exit
477 |         return n;
478 |       }
479 |     }
480 | 
481 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || result != null)) {
482 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
483 |       return n;
484 |     }
485 | 
486 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
487 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
488 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
489 |       Node replacement = IR.breakNode();
490 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, replacement);
491 |       this.reportCodeChange();
492 |       return replacement;
493 |     }
494 | 
495 |     return n;
496 |   }

/**
   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping
   * cases.
   */
Method code:
1014 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
1015 |     // unknown
1016 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
1017 |       return true;
1018 |     }
1019 |     // equality
1020 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
1021 |       return true;
1022 |     }
1023 |     // all type
1024 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
1025 |       return true;
1026 |     }

1028 |     if (thatType.isUnionType()) {
1029 |       UnionType union = thatType.toMaybeUnionType();
1030 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
1031 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
1032 |           return true;
1033 |         }
1034 |       }
1035 |     }
1036 |     // proxy types
1037 |     if (thatType instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
1038 |       return thisType.isSubtype(
1039 |           ((ProxyObjectType) thatType).getReferencedTypeInternal());
1040 |     }
1041 |     return false;
1042 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(Node)

/**
   * @return Whether the Node is a DO or FUNCTION (with or without
   * labels).
   */
Method code:
861 |   private boolean isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(Node n) {
862 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
863 |       Node labeledStatement = n.getLastChild();
864 |       if (!labeledStatement.isBlock()) {
865 |         return isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(labeledStatement);
866 |       } else {
867 |         // For labels with block children, we need to ensure that a
868 |         // labeled FUNCTION or DO isn't generated when extraneous BLOCKs
869 |         // are skipped.
870 |         if (getNonEmptyChildCount(n, 2) == 1) {
871 |           return isOneExactlyFunctionOrDo(getFirstNonEmptyChild(n));
872 |         } else {
873 |           // Either a empty statement or an block with more than one child,
874 |           // way it isn't a FUNCTION or DO.
875 |           return false;
876 |         }
877 |       }
878 |     } else {
879 |       return (n.isFunction() || n.isDo());
880 |     }
881 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PureFunctionIdentifier.getCallableDefinitions(DefinitionProvider,Node)

/**
   * Query the DefinitionProvider for the list of definitions that
   * correspond to a given qualified name subtree.  Return null if
   * DefinitionProvider does not contain an entry for a given name,
   * one or more of the values returned by getDeclarations is not
   * callable, or the "name" node is not a GETPROP or NAME.
   *
   * @param definitionProvider The name reference graph
   * @param name Query node
   * @return non-empty definition list or null
   */
Method code:
189 |   private static Collection<Definition> getCallableDefinitions(
190 |       DefinitionProvider definitionProvider, Node name) {
191 |     if (name.isGetProp() || name.isName()) {
192 |       List<Definition> result = Lists.newArrayList();
193 | 
194 |       Collection<Definition> decls =
195 |           definitionProvider.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(name);
196 |       if (decls == null) {
197 |         return null;
198 |       }
199 | 
200 |       for (Definition current : decls) {
201 |         Node rValue = current.getRValue();
202 |         if ((rValue != null) && rValue.isFunction()) {
203 |           result.add(current);
204 |         } else {
205 |           return null;
206 |         }
207 |       }
208 | 
209 |       return result;
210 |     } else if (name.isOr() || name.isHook()) {
211 |       Node firstVal;
212 |       if (name.isHook()) {
213 |         firstVal = name.getFirstChild().getNext();
214 |       } else {
215 |         firstVal = name.getFirstChild();
216 |       }
217 | 
218 |       Collection<Definition> defs1 = getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider,
219 |                                                             firstVal);
220 |       Collection<Definition> defs2 = getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider,
221 |                                                             firstVal.getNext());
222 |       if (defs1 != null && defs2 != null) {
223 |         defs1.addAll(defs2);
224 |         return defs1;
225 |       } else {
226 |         return null;
227 |       }
228 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(name)) {
229 |       // The anonymous function reference is also the definition.
230 |       // TODO(user) Change SimpleDefinitionFinder so it is possible to query for
231 |       // function expressions by function node.
232 | 
233 |       // isExtern is false in the call to the constructor for the
234 |       // FunctionExpressionDefinition below because we know that
235 |       // getCallableDefinitions() will only be called on the first
236 |       // child of a call and thus the function expression
237 |       // definition will never be an extern.
238 |       return Lists.newArrayList(
239 |           (Definition)
240 |               new DefinitionsRemover.FunctionExpressionDefinition(name, false));
241 |     } else {
242 |       return null;
243 |     }
244 |   }
